$comment: Generated by scripts/GenerateManifest.mjs from docs/, docs/generated/props.json, the example files and the tokens; do not edit. Paths are relative to the package root.
rule: Search envUI before writing any UI element; propose an envUI addition instead of a local copy.

components.name: Stack
components.summary: Stack lays out content in a column, or a row, with even gaps, such as a form and its actions.
useWhen: Content runs top to bottom with even space between, such as a heading, text and a form.
Sections and their contents need different spacing, by nesting stacks with different gaps.
A few actions belong together, such as a form's Cancel and Save, in a row that wraps.
Actions in a narrow pane need the whole width for their labels, stacked with fullWidth buttons.

avoidWhen.text: Buttons joined into one connected control, such as a main action beside a menu of alternatives.
Controls for one subject that the arrow keys move between, such as an editor's formatting.
A background, an inset and corners around content.
A block with a heading, metadata and actions.
Rows of items with labels, descriptions and actions.
Content in columns or a grid; lay it out in the application's CSS with the spacing tokens.
The frame of an application, with a header and a sidebar.

examples.name: ProjectDetails
examples.title: Stack
examples.description: Stack lays out content in a column, or a row, with even gaps, such as a form and its actions.

examples.name: NestedSpacing
examples.title: Spacing sections and their content
examples.description: A larger gap between sections and a smaller one inside them group what belongs together.

examples.name: CenteredContent
examples.title: Centred content
examples.description: `align="center"` keeps each child at its own width in the middle of the column.

examples.name: FormActions
examples.title: Form actions
examples.description: `render` lays out the form as the stack. A row with `render={<footer />}` and `justify="end"` puts the actions at the end of the form.

examples.name: StackedActions
examples.title: Stacked actions
examples.description: In a narrow pane, a column of buttons with `fullWidth` gives each label the whole width.

components.name: Page
components.summary: The column a page's content sits in, centered at one of four widths with the page gutter, and the page's header at its top.
useWhen: A page's content needs a readable width in a wide window, such as a form, a document or a dashboard.
A page has a heading with actions above its content, passed as its header.

avoidWhen.text: The frame of an application, with its header and sidebars.
Content in a column or a row with even gaps inside a page.
A background, an inset and corners around a part of a page.
Two panes side by side that people resize.

examples.name: WithHeader
examples.title: Page
examples.description: The column a page's content sits in, centered at one of four widths with the page gutter, and the page's header at its top.

examples.name: Widths
examples.title: Widths
examples.description: The four widths, in a muted surface that shows the space around the column.

components.name: PageHeader
components.summary: A page's heading row, with its title, an optional trail and description, its actions and a toolbar row, that wraps to its own width and can stick to the top.
useWhen: A page opens with its title and the actions that apply to the whole page, such as New project.
A page needs its trail, a status or a count beside its title, or a row of search and filters under it.
The page's heading should stay in view as the page scrolls.

avoidWhen.text: The application's header across every page, with its sidebar toggle and account menu.
The heading of a section inside a page, with its own actions.
A heading with metadata and actions around a block of content.
Controls for one subject that the arrow keys move between.

examples.name: WithBreadcrumbs
examples.title: PageHeader
examples.description: A page's heading row, with its title, an optional trail and description, its actions and a toolbar row, that wraps to its own width and can stick to the top.

examples.name: WithToolbar
examples.title: Search and filters
examples.description: A toolbar row under the title holds the search field and a view switch, with small controls.

examples.name: Sticky
examples.title: Sticky
examples.description: The header stays at the top as the page scrolls under it.

examples.name: InANarrowPane
examples.title: In a narrow pane
examples.description: In a side panel the actions move under the title and wrap; an avatar leads the title.

components.name: SplitPane
components.summary: Two panes with a handle between them that people drag or move with the arrow keys, and ListDetail, a list beside the detail of its chosen item.
useWhen: Two related panes share a region and people size them to their task, such as a source beside its preview.
A list sits beside the detail of the chosen item, and shows one at a time on a narrow screen.

avoidWhen.text: The application's sidebar, which collapses and opens as a drawer on a phone.
A panel docked at an edge of the window over the page.
Content that simply follows, without a handle.
Columns of a table that people resize.

examples.name: ResizablePanes
examples.title: SplitPane
examples.description: Two panes with a handle between them that people drag or move with the arrow keys, and ListDetail, a list beside the detail of its chosen item.

examples.name: Persisted
examples.title: A persisted width
examples.description: A rem-sized outline that keeps its width under a localStorage key.

examples.name: MasterDetail
examples.title: A list and its detail
examples.description: ListDetail shows people beside the chosen person's details; in a narrow space, one at a time.

components.name: Surface
components.summary: A container with a background, an inset and corners, but no layout of its own.
useWhen: A region needs a background, an inset and corners, such as a detail pane or a side panel.
A block should stand apart from what is around it, such as a raised summary on a pane.
A toolbar floats over dense content, such as a diagram, with small controls inside.

avoidWhen.text: Content with a heading, metadata and actions, or a block people press to open something.
Rows of items that people scan, each with a label, a description and actions.
Space between children without a background.
Content over the page that people dismiss, such as a form in a window.
A floating panel that opens from a button.

examples.name: DetailPane
examples.title: Surface
examples.description: A container with a background, an inset and corners, but no layout of its own.

examples.name: RaisedOnPane
examples.title: A raised block on a pane
examples.description: `background="raised"` sets a block apart on a pane; `sm` corners suit its smaller size.

examples.name: Toolbar
examples.title: Toolbar
examples.description: A pill surface holds controls over dense content, with controls of size `sm`. `render` lays them out as a row, and `role="group"` with a label names them together. For a toolbar the arrow keys move through, render the surface as a Toolbar.

components.name: List
components.summary: A vertical list of connected rows, each with a title, a detail and an action, that can open what it names, show the current one and be put in order.
useWhen: Related items with a title, a short detail and an action each, such as the sections of a settings page.
Items that each open a page or a document, such as recent plans (`interactive`).
A short set of results or members under a search field.
The list beside an item's details, with its current row marked (`selected`).
Items people put in their own order, such as the slides of a deck or an agenda (`onReorder`).

avoidWhen.text: Data compared across columns, or rows people sort by a value.
Destinations in an application's navigation.
A hierarchy people expand, such as folders.
One choice from a few options shown as rows.
Content about one subject that stands on its own.

examples.name: SettingsRows
examples.title: List
examples.description: A vertical list of connected rows, each with a title, a detail and an action, that can open what it names, show the current one and be put in order.

examples.name: OpenFromRow
examples.title: Rows that open something
examples.description: Each title link covers its row, so a press anywhere on the row opens the plan; the More actions button stays above it and names its row.

examples.name: OnAPane
examples.title: Rows on a pane
examples.description: A muted Surface that holds only the list puts the rows on a pane of their own, in the raised row fill.

examples.name: CurrentRow
examples.title: The current row
examples.description: An avatar leads each row, and choosing a person marks their row as the current one, as for a list beside the person's details.

examples.name: CheckedRows
examples.title: Checked rows
examples.description: A checkbox in the start slot chooses rows for an action on several at once, and a checked row takes the selected fill.

examples.name: Reorder
examples.title: Put in order
examples.description: With `onReorder`, each row gets a handle: drag it, or press <kbd>Space</kbd> on it and move the row with the arrow keys. The list reports the move, and the application moves the item.

examples.name: ExtraContent
examples.title: More content in a row
examples.description: Children follow the title and the detail, such as a Badge with the item's status.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A rounded surface that groups content about one subject, as a content card with a heading and actions, a feature card, or one link or button.
useWhen: Content about one subject stands apart from the page, such as a project's summary.
A summary needs its own actions along the bottom, such as Share and Open (`actions`).
The whole surface leads to one destination or starts one action, such as a project in a grid (`href`, `onClick`).
A feature is introduced with an icon, a sentence and one action (`layout="feature"`).

avoidWhen.text: A fill, padding and corners without card semantics or spacing, such as a toolbar's background.
Rows of items with a label, a description and an action, connected in one list.
Data to compare across rows and columns.
A message about the page or a section.
A region with no content yet.

examples.name: ProjectSummary
examples.title: Card
examples.description: A rounded surface that groups content about one subject, as a content card with a heading and actions, a feature card, or one link or button.

examples.name: ActionStrip
examples.title: Action strip
examples.description: `heading`, `meta` and `actions` make a heading row and a strip of controls along the bottom; `render` makes the card an article.

examples.name: Destinations
examples.title: Link cards
examples.description: Each card is one link, named by its title and summary, in a grid of as many columns as fit.

examples.name: StartOptions
examples.title: Button cards
examples.description: A button card starts an action, here one way to start a project; a disabled one cannot be pressed.

examples.name: FeatureCards
examples.title: Feature cards
examples.description: The feature layout presents a feature with an icon and one action, and stacks them when the card is narrow.

components.name: Button
components.summary: Starts an action, or goes to a destination with href, alone, icon-only, confirmed in place, copying a value or connected in a group.
useWhen: Someone starts an action, such as saving, creating or sending.
A prominent destination, such as the next step of a flow, should look like an action.
An icon alone names a familiar action in a dense place, such as a toolbar (IconButton).
An action takes effect at once and cannot be undone, such as removing someone's access (ConfirmButton).
People copy a value to paste elsewhere, such as a link, an ID or a command (CopyButton).
Related actions belong together, such as the main action and a menu of alternatives (ButtonGroup).

avoidWhen.text: A destination inside running text.
Choosing one of a few views or filters that stays selected.
A setting that turns on or off.
A list of actions that would crowd a toolbar.
A consequence that needs a choice or typed confirmation before it happens.

examples.name: CreateProject
examples.title: Button
examples.description: Starts an action, or goes to a destination with href, alone, icon-only, confirmed in place, copying a value or connected in a group.

examples.name: Variants
examples.title: Variants
examples.description: One primary action per group; the others step down in emphasis.

examples.name: Icons
examples.title: Icons
examples.description: `startIcon` and `endIcon` add decorative icons beside the label. An icon-only button, IconButton or Button with `iconOnly`, needs an `aria-label`.

examples.name: QuietToolbar
examples.title: Ghost actions in chrome
examples.description: Ghost buttons suit an application's chrome, such as a sidebar toggle or a section's actions inside a surface: the icon color, with a state layer on hover and press.

examples.name: ButtonLinks
examples.title: Destinations
examples.description: With `href` a button is a native link. Text buttons read as links; `underline` adds an underline.

examples.name: PendingAction
examples.title: Pending work
examples.description: A pending button keeps its size, shows a spinner and ignores repeated presses until the work ends.

examples.name: SayWhatWillHappen
examples.title: Say what will happen
examples.description: Put the outcome in the label when it is known. AnimatedNumber rolls a count that changes while choices are made.

examples.name: ConfirmInPlace
examples.title: Confirm in place
examples.description: ConfirmButton names the consequence on the first press and acts on the second. It disarms after a few seconds, when focus leaves and on <kbd>Esc</kbd>.

examples.name: CopyValue
examples.title: Copy to the clipboard
examples.description: After a press the icon turns into a check, and Copied shows and is announced for about two seconds.

examples.name: CustomClipboard
examples.title: Your own clipboard
examples.description: `write` copies through the application's own clipboard, here a stand-in that takes a moment; the button shows the result as it does for the browser's.

examples.name: ConnectedButtons
examples.title: Connected buttons
examples.description: ButtonGroup connects related actions in a row or a column. Prefer the same variant within a group; mix variants when related actions need different emphasis.

examples.name: FillSidebar
examples.title: Fill a sidebar
examples.description: With `fullWidth` a group fills its container: the labelled button takes the room the menu's chevron leaves.

components.name: CloseButton
components.summary: The icon-only button that closes, dismisses or removes what it sits in, named Close in the application's language.
useWhen: A panel, a notification or a tip closes or is dismissed in place.
A list of items, such as people or files, lets each be removed.

avoidWhen.text: A dialog's own close, which Dialog renders itself.
An action that deletes something for good, which needs its consequence named.
Any other icon-only action.

examples.name: DismissTip
examples.title: CloseButton
examples.description: The icon-only button that closes, dismisses or removes what it sits in, named Close in the application's language.

examples.name: RemovePeople
examples.title: Remove items
examples.description: Beside others like it, each button names what it removes.

examples.name: TranslatedLabel
examples.title: Translated name
examples.description: An EnvUIProvider's `messages` name every CloseButton inside it.

components.name: SearchTrigger
components.summary: The button that opens search or a command palette, with its ⌘K or Ctrl+K shortcut, as a field-like row or an icon.
useWhen: Search or a command palette opens from a button at the top of a sidebar or in a header.
The application opens search with a keyboard shortcut and shows it where people look for search.
A narrow header or a sidebar showing icons only needs search as an icon.

avoidWhen.text: People type the search on the page itself and the results filter in place.
The search itself, with its field and results.

examples.name: InSidebar
examples.title: SearchTrigger
examples.description: The button that opens search or a command palette, with its ⌘K or Ctrl+K shortcut, as a field-like row or an icon.

examples.name: IconOnly
examples.title: Icon only
examples.description: In a narrow header, the trigger shows only its icon, with the label and the keys in its tooltip. It doesn't listen, since the sidebar's trigger already opens the same search.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A row, or a column, of controls for one subject, one tab stop from the page, moved through with the arrow keys.
useWhen: A set of controls acts on one subject, such as an editor's formatting or a diagram's view.
Many icon-only actions sit together and would make a long tab sequence one by one.
A tool is chosen from a palette and stays chosen, such as a drawing tool.

avoidWhen.text: A form's or a dialog's actions, which keep a tab stop each.
Buttons joined into one connected control, such as a main action and its menu.
A choice of one view or filter, shown as a selected segment.
An application's menus of commands, such as File and Edit.
A page's search, filters and primary action, where fields keep their arrow keys.

examples.name: FormattingToolbar
examples.title: Toolbar
examples.description: A row, or a column, of controls for one subject, one tab stop from the page, moved through with the arrow keys.

examples.name: ViewControls
examples.title: Diagram controls
examples.description: A pill Surface rendered as the toolbar floats it over a diagram, with small buttons and a link to help.

examples.name: DrawingTools
examples.title: Drawing tools
examples.description: A vertical toolbar of toggles, where one tool stays chosen.

examples.name: PageToolbar
examples.title: Page toolbar
examples.description: A page's search and filter under its title, with the primary action at the end of the row: a Stack row in PageHeader's `toolbar`, not a Toolbar.

examples.name: SectionToolbar
examples.title: Section toolbar
examples.description: A section's heading and count at the start and its actions at the end, wrapping when there isn't room.

examples.name: TableToolbar
examples.title: Table toolbar
examples.description: Small controls above a table of small rows, so the bar and the rows share one density.

components.name: Link
components.summary: A destination inside running text, underlined by default, routed by the application.
useWhen: A destination inside a sentence or a paragraph, such as a guide or a related page.
A short list of destinations where buttons would be too heavy, with the underline turned off.

avoidWhen.text: An action, such as saving or deleting, even when it looks like text.
The next step of a flow, which should read as an action.
Destinations in an application's navigation, such as a sidebar.
Previous and next pages of a sequence.

examples.name: InRunningText
examples.title: Link
examples.description: A destination inside running text, underlined by default, routed by the application.

examples.name: WithoutUnderline
examples.title: Without an underline
examples.description: Where the context already marks the words as links, `underline={false}` leaves the link color alone.

components.name: ColorPicker
components.summary: A color area, a hue slider and a HEX field for choosing an opaque color, and a color swatch that shows one.
useWhen: People choose any opaque color, such as an accent or a label's color, by eye or by its HEX value.
A button or a list shows a color that people chose, as a round sample (ColorSwatch).

avoidWhen.text: Choosing one of a few named colors or themes.
Choosing one of a fixed list of colors with names.
A light, dark or system appearance.

examples.name: AccentColor
examples.title: ColorPicker
examples.description: A color area, a hue slider and a HEX field for choosing an opaque color, and a color swatch that shows one.

examples.name: SwatchButton
examples.title: Open from a swatch
examples.description: A secondary button shows the color as a swatch and its HEX value, and opens the picker in a Popover.

examples.name: ProjectColorForm
examples.title: In a form
examples.description: `name` submits the HEX value with the form, and Reset returns an uncontrolled picker to its `defaultValue`.

examples.name: Swatches
examples.title: Swatches beside names
examples.description: ColorSwatch shows each label's color before its name, with the value written beside it; a white swatch keeps its ring.

components.name: TextField
components.summary: Single-line inputs, search fields and multiline textareas share labels, guidance and states.
useWhen: Someone types a short value on one line, such as a name, an e-mail address or a number.
A value has a fixed start or a unit beside it, such as an address after a domain or a size in GB.
People search or filter a list, a table or a sidebar by typing (SearchField).
Someone writes text over several lines, such as a description or notes (Textarea).

avoidWhen.text: Text that runs over several lines.
A query that searches or filters content, which needs a search icon and a way to clear it.
Choosing one of a few known options.
Choosing from a long list of options by typing to filter them.
A date, or a date and time.
A message in a conversation, sent with Enter.
Formatted text, such as headings, lists and links.

examples.name: ProjectName
examples.title: TextField
examples.description: Single-line inputs, search fields and multiline textareas share labels, guidance and states.

examples.name: Variants
examples.title: Appearances
examples.description: Outline fields suit forms, underline fields a title in a document or a header, and ghost fields a search at the top of a sidebar.

examples.name: Validation
examples.title: Show an error
examples.description: The description states the rule and the error says how to correct the value. Here the field is checked once people leave it, and the error goes as soon as the value fits.

examples.name: PrefixAndSuffix
examples.title: Prefix and suffix
examples.description: Short text in line with the value, such as the start of an address or a unit; forms submit only the value. It appears once the field has focus or a value, and always beside the placeholder of a field whose label is hidden.

examples.name: IconAndAction
examples.title: Icon and end action
examples.description: `startIcon` adds a decorative icon at the start; `endAction` holds a control at the end, here an IconButton that shows the password, which takes the ghost look of the field.

examples.name: FieldsBesideButtons
examples.title: Fields beside buttons
examples.description: Fields share the button height of their size. Without a visible label the placeholder guides; with its label shown, the label rests inside and floats into the outline without changing the height.

examples.name: FilterList
examples.title: Search a list
examples.description: SearchField filters as people type; its clear button and <kbd>Esc</kbd> clear the query. A status line announces how many members match.

examples.name: SidebarSearch
examples.title: Search a sidebar
examples.description: A ghost SearchField at the top of a sidebar shows only its icon and placeholder until the pointer or focus gives it a soft fill.

examples.name: TextareaSizing
examples.title: Textarea sizing
examples.description: A fixed Textarea scrolls its text; drag its bottom edge, or focus the edge and use the arrow keys, to resize it. With `sizing="content"` and `rows={1}`, a reply starts at one line and grows with its text.

components.name: Field
components.summary: The parts of a labelled form field, a label, a control, a description and an error, for a control envUI has no field for.
useWhen: A control of the application's own needs a label, a description and an error, wired for assistive technology.
A form validates a value on blur or on submit with the browser's validity or a function of its own.

avoidWhen.text: A single-line text input with a label, a description and an error.
A choice from a list.
Text over several lines.
A choice that turns on or off.

examples.name: ProjectName
examples.title: Field
examples.description: The parts of a labelled form field, a label, a control, a description and an error, for a control envUI has no field for.

examples.name: ValidateOnBlur
examples.title: Validate on blur
examples.description: `validate` checks the value as focus leaves the control, and the error shows the message it returns.

examples.name: ApplicationControl
examples.title: A control of the application's own
examples.description: `render` takes any control, such as a native range input, which the label and the description describe.

components.name: Composer
components.summary: The message field of a conversation, which grows with its text and sends with Enter, with a send button that stops a running reply.
useWhen: People write a message in a conversation, such as a chat, a comment thread or a prompt, and send it with Enter.
A reply runs after a message is sent and people may stop it (`running`, `onStop`).

avoidWhen.text: Text over several lines in a form, where Enter starts a new line.
One line of text in a form.
Formatted text with headings, lists and links.
A query that searches or filters content.

examples.name: AskAnything
examples.title: Composer
examples.description: The message field of a conversation, which grows with its text and sends with Enter, with a send button that stops a running reply.

examples.name: StartAndFooter
examples.title: Start content and a footer
examples.description: Start content moves the send button to an action row below the field; the footer describes the field.

examples.name: PendingSend
examples.title: Pending send
examples.description: While the reply is sent, `pending` holds the next send; the field stays editable and keeps focus.

examples.name: FormSubmit
examples.title: Sent by its form
examples.description: Without `onSubmit`, <kbd>Enter</kbd> and the send button submit the form, which sends the text under `name`.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A native checkbox with its label, for a choice people turn on or off on its own, with a mixed state for a group's parent.
useWhen: People choose any number of options from a list, each on its own, such as which e-mails to receive.
One option is agreed to or included, such as accepting the terms or including archived items, and takes effect when a form is sent.
A parent selects or clears a group of options and shows when only some are chosen (`checked="mixed"`).

avoidWhen.text: A setting that takes effect at once, such as turning notifications on.
Exactly one choice from a few options.
One choice from a long list of options.
Several choices from a long list, found by typing.
Choosing rows of a table.

examples.name: IncludeArchived
examples.title: Checkbox
examples.description: A native checkbox with its label, for a choice people turn on or off on its own, with a mixed state for a group's parent.

examples.name: SelectAll
examples.title: Select all
examples.description: The parent is checked when every project is, mixed when some are, and checks or clears them all when pressed. The children line up with the parent's label.

examples.name: NotificationForm
examples.title: In a form
examples.description: Checkboxes with the same `name` submit one entry for each checked value. A fieldset's legend names the group, and Reset returns every box to `defaultChecked`.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: An on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it changes.
useWhen: A setting turns on or off and takes effect at once, such as e-mail notifications or showing completed tasks.
Each row of a settings list turns one setting on or off.

avoidWhen.text: A choice that waits for a Save or Submit button, such as accepting terms, or one of several options people tick.
Choosing between two or more named views or modes, such as List and Board.
Choosing one of several options in a form.
An action that runs once, such as archiving a project.
An option that turns on or off inside a menu.

examples.name: NotificationSettings
examples.title: Switch
examples.description: An on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it changes.

examples.name: ShowCompleted
examples.title: Apply at once
examples.description: The list follows the switch as soon as it changes; there is nothing to save.

examples.name: SettingsRows
examples.title: Settings in a list
examples.description: Each row's switch is named by the row's title and described by its detail, so the visible text is read once.

examples.name: ManagedSetting
examples.title: Unavailable settings
examples.description: Disabled switches keep their state visible. A sentence linked to both with `aria-describedby` says why they can't change.

components.name: Radio
components.summary: One choice from a few options shown together, side by side or as selectable rows.
useWhen: People choose exactly one of two to five options, and seeing them all helps them choose, such as who can open a project.
Each option needs a sentence that explains it, such as a role or a visibility (`orientation="vertical"`).
A choice in a form or a dialog that takes effect when the form is saved.

avoidWhen.text: More options than fit comfortably, or options people already know, such as a country or a time zone.
Finding one option in a long list by typing.
Switching between views or filters that apply at once, such as List and Board.
Several options people can choose together, or one option on its own.
A setting that turns on or off and applies at once.

examples.name: ProjectAccess
examples.title: Radio
examples.description: One choice from a few options shown together, side by side or as selectable rows.

examples.name: VisibilityRows
examples.title: Selectable rows
examples.description: Rows suit options that need a sentence each. The disabled option says why in its description.

examples.name: RequiredChoice
examples.title: A required choice
examples.description: The group starts with nothing chosen. Exporting without a choice shows an error linked to the group, announces it and moves focus to the first option.

examples.name: InheritedAccess
examples.title: A choice that can't change here
examples.description: A disabled group keeps its choice visible, and a sentence linked with `aria-describedby` says where to change it.

components.name: Select
components.summary: One choice from a list that stays collapsed until opened, on a Button-style trigger with a label, description and error.
useWhen: People choose one of several known options, such as a role, a sort order or a time zone, and the choice can stay collapsed.
A setting in a row or a toolbar takes one of a few values, such as an e-mail digest's frequency or a zoom level.

avoidWhen.text: Two to five options that read better side by side, or that each need explaining.
Finding one option in a long list by typing, or choosing several.
Switching between views or filters that apply at once, such as List and Board.
A list of actions, such as Rename or Delete, rather than a value.
A date, or a date and time.

examples.name: ProjectVisibility
examples.title: Select
examples.description: One choice from a list that stays collapsed until opened, on a Button-style trigger with a label, description and error.

examples.name: TriggerStyles
examples.title: Trigger styles
examples.description: The secondary trigger fills on the page; the outline one keeps a border on a pane, where a fill would blend in.

examples.name: InviteMember
examples.title: In a form
examples.description: The label sits above a trigger that fits its content, beside a full-width text field. The description says what the roles mean, and `name` submits the chosen role with the form.

examples.name: SettingRows
examples.title: In list rows
examples.description: A row's title names its select with `aria-label`; outline triggers stay distinct on the row fill.

examples.name: SmallToolbar
examples.title: Small, in a toolbar
examples.description: A small, outline select fits a toolbar beside small text icon buttons. Its list has a check mark on the chosen zoom level.

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.summary: One choice among a few items on a pill rail, such as views or filters of the same content.
useWhen: People switch between two to five views or filters of the same content, such as Open, Blocked and Done items, and the choice applies at once.
A toolbar switches how content is laid out, such as List and Board (`size="sm"`).
A narrow container, such as a sidebar, holds a choice between two scopes (`fullWidth`).

avoidWhen.text: Each option has a panel of its own, such as the sections of a settings page.
A choice in a form that is saved with it, or options that need explaining.
More than five options, or options with long names.
A setting that turns on or off.
Actions, such as Save and Share, rather than a choice that stays selected.

examples.name: WorkItems
examples.title: SegmentedControl
examples.description: One choice among a few items on a pill rail, such as views or filters of the same content.

examples.name: SmallToolbar
examples.title: Small, in a toolbar
examples.description: `size="sm"` makes the rail as tall as the small button beside it. Timeline is disabled, and the arrow keys skip it.

examples.name: FillSidebar
examples.title: Fill a sidebar
examples.description: With `fullWidth` the control fills a sidebar and splits it between the options. Labels too long for their half end with an ellipsis and show whole in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus.

components.name: Combobox
components.summary: A text field that filters a list of options as people type, to choose one option or, as chips, several.
useWhen: People choose one option from a list long enough to search, such as an owner among a team's members.
People choose several options from such a list, which show as chips in the field (`multiple`).
The options come from a search, such as contacts on a server (`filter={null}`).

avoidWhen.text: Choosing one of a handful of options, which people can scan without typing.
Typing a query that searches or filters content on the page.
Free text that is not one of the options, such as a name.
One of two to five options shown side by side.
Finding and running a command or opening a document by name.

examples.name: ChooseOwner
examples.title: Combobox
examples.description: A text field that filters a list of options as people type, to choose one option or, as chips, several.

examples.name: Reviewers
examples.title: Several reviewers
examples.description: With `multiple`, chosen people show as chips in the field; <kbd>Backspace</kbd> in the empty text removes the last one.

examples.name: SmallToolbar
examples.title: Small, in a toolbar
examples.description: `size="sm"` gives the field the small control height, so it lines up with a small button beside it. Without a visible label, its placeholder guides; the popup groups its options under headings.

examples.name: ServerSearch
examples.title: Search on a server
examples.description: With `filter={null}` the list shows the people the application finds for the typed text, with a loading status while it searches.

examples.name: RequiredInForm
examples.title: In a form
examples.description: A multiple combobox submits one entry for each chosen topic. The application checks that one is chosen and shows the error; Reset returns to `defaultValue`.

components.name: DatePicker
components.summary: A field that opens a calendar to choose a date, or a date and time, and the calendar on its own.
useWhen: People choose a day, such as when a report goes out or a task is due.
People choose a day and a time, such as when a meeting starts (`granularity="minute"`).
A day is chosen within a page or a panel from a month that stays visible, such as in a planning view (Calendar).

avoidWhen.text: A moment shown relative to now, such as "3 hours ago".
Activity per day over months, shown as shades.
A free-text date that people type in any format.
A choice among a few named periods, such as This week or This month.

examples.name: PublishDate
examples.title: DatePicker
examples.description: A field that opens a calendar to choose a date, or a date and time, and the calendar on its own.

examples.name: MeetingTime
examples.title: A date and a time
examples.description: With `granularity="minute"`, the calendar stays open for the time field; Now chooses the current date and time, and Done closes it.

examples.name: WithinRange
examples.title: Within a range
examples.description: `min` and `max` make the days outside this quarter unavailable, and the month buttons stop at them.

examples.name: SmallToolbar
examples.title: Small, in a toolbar
examples.description: `size="sm"` gives the field the small control height, so it lines up with small buttons, and its placeholder shows in place of the hidden label.

examples.name: LeaveRequest
examples.title: In a form
examples.description: Two required fields submit their days; the application checks their order and shows the error, and Reset returns them to `defaultValue`.

examples.name: PlanningCalendar
examples.title: A calendar on its own
examples.description: Calendar chooses a day within the page, named by `aria-label`; a status says which day is chosen.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: A value in a known range, chosen by dragging a thumb, pressing the track or with the keyboard.
useWhen: People adjust a value by eye within a known range, such as opacity, volume or zoom, and see the result as they move it.
The exact number matters less than its place in the range, and the value shows beside the label as it changes.

avoidWhen.text: People know the exact number they want, such as a price or a quantity.
Choosing one of a few named levels, such as Low, Medium and High.
Showing a measurement people don't change, such as storage used.
Showing how far a task has got.

examples.name: LayerOpacity
examples.title: Slider
examples.description: A value in a known range, chosen by dragging a thumb, pressing the track or with the keyboard.

examples.name: SaveOnRelease
examples.title: Save once a change is complete
examples.description: The value follows the thumb as it moves, and `onValueCommitted` saves it once, when the thumb is released or after a key. A status line announces the save.

examples.name: SessionTimeout
examples.title: Steps in a form
examples.description: `min`, `max` and `step` give whole 5-minute steps from 5 to 120, and `name` submits the value with the form. Reset returns the slider to `defaultValue`.

examples.name: ManagedLimit
examples.title: A value people can't change
examples.description: A disabled slider keeps its value visible, and the description says who sets it.

components.name: DropZone
components.summary: An area that takes dropped files and opens the file picker when pressed; the application handles and shows the files.
useWhen: People add a file to a form or a page, such as a logo, by dropping it or choosing it.
People attach several files at once, such as documents to a message (`multiple`, `size="sm"`).

avoidWhen.text: A text value people type, such as a link to a file.
A single action that opens the file picker in a toolbar, without a drop target.
Progress of a long upload with a known size.

examples.name: LogoUpload
examples.title: DropZone
examples.description: An area that takes dropped files and opens the file picker when pressed; the application handles and shows the files.

examples.name: AttachDocuments
examples.title: Attach several files
examples.description: A small zone with `multiple` adds documents to a list the application shows, each with a Remove action.

examples.name: UploadProgress
examples.title: Upload with progress
examples.description: While the application uploads a file, the zone is pending, its label says what is happening, and a status announces when it's done.

examples.name: InAForm
examples.title: In a form
examples.description: With `name`, the form submits the files the zone took, and Reset clears them.

components.name: NavList
components.summary: A list of navigation destinations, such as the pages in a sidebar, with icons, counts, groups and an icon-only form.
useWhen: An application's main destinations, such as the pages in a sidebar.
The pages of an area listed beside its content, such as the sections of a guide or of the account settings.
A collapsed sidebar or a rail that shows only icons, with the labels in tooltips (iconOnly).

avoidWhen.text: Switching between views of the same content in one place.
A short list of actions or destinations behind one control.
The path from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page.
The previous and next pages of an ordered sequence, such as a guide.
A deep hierarchy that people expand and collapse, such as folders and files.
Choosing one of a few filters or modes that stays selected.

examples.name: SidebarNavigation
examples.title: NavList
examples.description: A list of navigation destinations, such as the pages in a sidebar, with icons, counts, groups and an icon-only form.

examples.name: GroupedDestinations
examples.title: Grouped destinations
examples.description: NavList.Group puts related pages under a small heading, which also names the group's list. Without icons, the headings line up with the labels.

examples.name: InACompactRegion
examples.title: In a compact region
examples.description: Items follow the app's scale. A Theme with `scale="compact"` around a whole region, such as a docked list of recent documents, gives its items the compact height and labels.

examples.name: CollapsedSidebar
examples.title: Collapsed sidebar
examples.description: With `iconOnly` the items show only their icons and their labels in tooltips; the count turns into a dot, so the item's `aria-label` carries it. The label stays as children for the expanded sidebar.

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: Switches between panels of related content in one place, from a rail of buttons.
useWhen: Related views of one subject in one place, such as a project's summary, details and activity.
Content that splits into sections people look at one at a time, such as the parts of a settings page.
Views that fill a region, such as a diagram's canvas and its outline (fill).

avoidWhen.text: A filter or mode that changes the content below, such as a list's sort order or a chart's range.
Open documents that people close, reorder and keep, as in an editor.
An application's destinations, such as the pages in a sidebar.
Sections people may want open at the same time.

examples.name: ProjectViews
examples.title: Tabs
examples.description: Switches between panels of related content in one place, from a rail of buttons.

examples.name: ManualActivation
examples.title: Manual activation
examples.description: With `activation="manual"` the arrow keys move focus and <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> selects, so a report loads only when chosen.

examples.name: SmallRail
examples.title: Small rail
examples.description: `size="sm"` makes the rail as tall as a small control, for a toolbar or a bar; a CounterBadge fits inside a tab.

examples.name: FillARegion
examples.title: Fill a region
examples.description: With `fill` the selected panel takes the height left below the rail, here a region 16 rem tall.

examples.name: VerticalList
examples.title: Vertical list
examples.description: A vertical rail of NavList.Item tabs, with ↑ and ↓; the Tabs is laid out as a row to put the panels beside it.

examples.name: ListBesideAHeading
examples.title: List beside a heading
examples.description: `renderList` places the rail beside a heading inside a Card, and the panels follow below.

components.name: Pager
components.summary: Previous and next links between the pages of an ordered sequence, such as a guide, centered at the end of the content.
useWhen: The pages of an ordered sequence, such as a guide, a handbook or release notes, link to their neighbours after the content.
A reader moves on to the next page of reading content, and may go back a page.

avoidWhen.text: Moving through the pages of a long list or table.
The next step of a form or a task, such as Continue in a checkout.
An application's main destinations, such as the pages in a sidebar.
The path from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page.

examples.name: PreviousAndNext
examples.title: Pager
examples.description: Previous and next links between the pages of an ordered sequence, such as a guide, centered at the end of the content.

examples.name: StepThroughAGuide
examples.title: Step through a guide
examples.description: On the first page only the next link shows; the previous link joins it from the second page on.

examples.name: ComposedParts
examples.title: Compose the parts
examples.description: Pager.Previous and Pager.Next as children of Pager.Root make the same pair, here without icons.

examples.name: LongTitles
examples.title: Long titles in a narrow column
examples.description: Where the pair doesn't fit side by side, each link takes a row of its own, and titles wrap between words.

components.name: AppShell
components.summary: The frame of a whole application, with a topbar, a collapsible navigation sidebar and the content area, or a window title bar.
useWhen: An application needs its frame, with a topbar with the page's title and actions, a navigation sidebar that collapses to icons, and the page's content.
An installed web app or desktop shell draws its own title bar over the window (`titleBar`, TitleBar).
The application's first load shows the frame before the data arrives (AppShellSkeleton).

avoidWhen.text: The destinations inside the sidebar.
A panel that opens beside the page for one item.
Items people keep open beside the page, such as drafts.
A region of a page with a fill and padding.

examples.name: ProductShell
examples.title: AppShell
examples.description: The frame of a whole application, with a topbar, a collapsible navigation sidebar and the content area, or a window title bar.

examples.name: TitleBarShell
examples.title: A title bar
examples.description: With `topbar="full"` and `titleBar`, the topbar is one row across the window that drags it: the mark, a menubar and a back button, the title and the actions.

examples.name: StartPageWindow
examples.title: A start page window
examples.description: TitleBar without the shell, inside a WindowFrame whose content scrolls below it.

examples.name: LoadingFrame
examples.title: The first load
examples.description: AppShellSkeleton shows the frame with placeholders until the application's data arrives.

components.name: Tree
components.summary: A virtualized tree of rows for large hierarchies, such as file trees, with keyboard navigation and a context menu.
useWhen: A hierarchy people expand and collapse, such as folders and files in a workspace's sidebar.
Thousands of rows, such as a large project's files, which the tree keeps fast by rendering only the rows in view.
Rows people preview with a click and open to keep with a double click, as in a desktop editor.

avoidWhen.text: An application's destinations, such as the pages in a sidebar, one or two levels deep.
A flat list of items, each with its own actions.
Records that share the same fields and that people compare.
Sections of content people show and hide in a page.

examples.name: FileTree
examples.title: Tree
examples.description: A virtualized tree of rows for large hierarchies, such as file trees, with keyboard navigation and a context menu.

examples.name: ContextMenuActions
examples.title: Actions in a context menu
examples.description: Right-click a row, or press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd>, for its actions, and the empty area for New document. The buttons above the tree offer the same actions.

examples.name: RowDensity
examples.title: Row density
examples.description: `density="md"` gives the rows more room than the default `sm`, here with counts at the end, a detail and a disabled mailbox. Only the padding changes; the text and icons stay the same.

examples.name: ThousandsOfRows
examples.title: Thousands of rows
examples.description: Expanding every folder makes over 10,000 rows; only those in view are in the document.

components.name: DocumentTabs
components.summary: Editor-style tabs for open documents, which people switch, close, pin and close all; the application renders the active document.
useWhen: People open several documents or files and switch between them, such as in an editor or a workspace.
Tabs open and close as people work, and one may be a preview until it is kept (`preview`, `onPin`).

avoidWhen.text: Switching between a fixed set of views of the same content, such as Overview and Settings.
Destinations in an application's navigation.
Choosing one of a few options or filters.
Items people keep open beside the page, such as drafts.

examples.name: OpenDocuments
examples.title: DocumentTabs
examples.description: Editor-style tabs for open documents, which people switch, close, pin and close all; the application renders the active document.

examples.name: ManyTabs
examples.title: Many open documents
examples.description: In a narrow pane the strip scrolls sideways, and the active tab stays in view.

components.name: PanelDock
components.summary: Panels docked side by side at the bottom of a region, for work beside the page, that minimize to chips and maximize while their content stays mounted.
useWhen: Items people work on beside the page and switch between, such as drafts, conversations or documents.
Work that must survive being set aside, such as an unsaved draft in a panel people minimize.
Several windows open at once in a workspace, which people minimize, maximize, resize and close.

avoidWhen.text: A task that needs an answer before people go on, or one panel beside the page that inspects it.
Switching between open documents in one place, as in an editor.
A short message about something that happened.

examples.name: DocumentDrafts
examples.title: PanelDock
examples.description: Panels docked side by side at the bottom of a region, for work beside the page, that minimize to chips and maximize while their content stays mounted.

examples.name: MaximizedPanel
examples.title: Maximized panel
examples.description: A maximized panel fills the region behind the open panels, which keep their modes; Restore returns it to the row.

examples.name: MinimizeWhatDoesNotFit
examples.title: Minimize what does not fit
examples.description: With `overflow="minimize"` three panels that can't sit side by side at 20 rem make room: the one active longest ago waits as a chip. It comes back once the region widens.

examples.name: NarrowRegion
examples.title: Narrow region
examples.description: Below `stackBelow` one panel at a time fills the region, here the active conversation, and its chip shows the other.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.summary: The path from the top level to the current page, with earlier levels as links or buttons.
useWhen: People move through a hierarchy and need to see where they are and go up, such as folders above a document.
A header or a bar names the current item's place in one line beside its status and actions (`wrap={false}`).

avoidWhen.text: The application's main navigation, such as the pages in a sidebar.
Moving between the items of one level, such as views of the same content.
Previous and next pages of a sequence.
Browsing and expanding a whole hierarchy.

examples.name: DocumentTrail
examples.title: Breadcrumbs
examples.description: The path from the top level to the current page, with earlier levels as links or buttons.

examples.name: WithoutUrls
examples.title: Applications without URLs
examples.description: Levels with `onClick` are buttons. Pressing one shortens the trail, and focus moves to the folder's title, since the pressed level becomes the current page.

examples.name: OneLine
examples.title: One line in a header bar
examples.description: With `wrap={false}` the trail stays on one line beside a status and an action; the current page is cut short first.

examples.name: LevelWithoutPage
examples.title: A level without a page
examples.description: An entry without `href` or `onClick` is plain text, for a level that can't be opened.

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: The range of items shown with previous and next page buttons, small enough for a toolbar.
useWhen: A long list or table read a page at a time, such as reports or invoices.
A list read in batches whose total isn't known yet, such as an activity feed.
A toolbar with little room for paging, beside a search field or filters.

avoidWhen.text: Links between the pages of an ordered sequence, such as the chapters of a guide.
Switching between a few views of the same content.

examples.name: PagesOfAList
examples.title: Pagination
examples.description: The range of items shown with previous and next page buttons, small enough for a toolbar.

examples.name: WithoutATotal
examples.title: Without a known total
examples.description: A list read in batches shows the items on the page; `hasNextPage` says when the list ends.

examples.name: SmallToolbar
examples.title: In a small toolbar
examples.description: `size="sm"` gives the buttons the small control height, as the field beside the pager has, and the field shrinks first. The text variant keeps the toolbar quiet.

examples.name: AnotherLanguage
examples.title: In another language
examples.description: EnvUIProvider's `messages.pagination` localizes every pager inside it and its `locale` formats the numbers; `previousLabel`, `nextLabel` and `formatRange` localize one pager. `lang` tells assistive technology the language.

components.name: AccountMenu
components.summary: The signed-in person's menu, opened from their avatar or a row with their name, with a header, a theme submenu and an optional organization submenu.
useWhen: The signed-in person's settings, theme and sign out, behind their avatar in a header or their name at the foot of a sidebar.
The theme choice, System, Light or Dark, in the account's menu rather than a toggle of its own.
Switching organizations from the account's menu, where the frame has no switcher of its own.

avoidWhen.text: A switch between organizations at the top of a sidebar, on its own.
Switching between the light and dark themes with one button.
Actions on an item or a view rather than on the account.

examples.name: ThemeAndOrganizations
examples.title: AccountMenu
examples.description: The signed-in person's menu, opened from their avatar or a row with their name, with a header, a theme submenu and an optional organization submenu.

examples.name: RowTrigger
examples.title: A row at the foot of a sidebar
examples.description: The row shows the name and the e-mail address, and opens the menu above it. The theme submenu here sets a theme the application stores itself, and closes the menu after the choice.

components.name: RichText
components.summary: Formatted text people edit as it looks, saved as Markdown with references, and shown again read-only.
useWhen: People write formatted text and see it as it will look, such as meeting notes, a brief or release notes.
Text mentions people, topics or files the application knows, saved with their IDs (references).
Formatted text saved earlier shows again read-only, rendered the same way, such as on a detail page (RichText).

avoidWhen.text: People edit Markdown source directly, with a preview.
Showing Markdown from anywhere, with the full CommonMark syntax, footnotes and plugins.
Plain text over several lines, without formatting.
A message in a conversation, sent with Enter.
A single line of text, such as a title.

examples.name: EditAndPreview
examples.title: RichText
examples.description: Formatted text people edit as it looks, saved as Markdown with references, and shown again read-only.

examples.name: SavedContent
examples.title: Show saved content
examples.description: RichText shows saved Markdown read-only. The application opens references and links through `onReferenceClick` and `onLinkClick`.

examples.name: References
examples.title: Mention people and topics
examples.description: Each reference source has a trigger, a name for its list and a lookup. Here a timer stands in for a search on a server, which the signal cancels when the query changes.

examples.name: SlashCommands
examples.title: Slash commands
examples.description: `slashCommands` adds a menu of blocks on /, and the application's own commands after them.

examples.name: UploadsAndLinks
examples.title: Attachments and links
examples.description: `onUpload` makes Attach files upload through the application, and `onRequestLink` replaces the link dialog with the application's own picker.

examples.name: EditorCommands
examples.title: Commands from outside
examples.description: `ref.editor` is the Tiptap editor, so the application can change the document with its commands.

examples.name: ReleaseNotesForm
examples.title: In a form
examples.description: With `name`, the form submits the Markdown. `error` says what to fix.

components.name: Markdown
components.summary: Renders a Markdown string in envUI's typography and code, and MarkdownEditor writes one with a toolbar and a preview.
useWhen: Content written in Markdown is shown, such as a saved description, a note or a document.
People write formatted prose as Markdown, with a toolbar and a preview of the result (MarkdownEditor).

avoidWhen.text: Plain text over several lines, without formatting.
Formatted text edited as it looks, without visible Markdown syntax.
A message in a conversation, sent with Enter.
Source code to read or copy on its own.

examples.name: ProjectNote
examples.title: Markdown
examples.description: Renders a Markdown string in envUI's typography and code, and MarkdownEditor writes one with a toolbar and a preview.

examples.name: EditDescription
examples.title: Write and preview
examples.description: MarkdownEditor with a label and a description grows with its text; the Preview tab renders it two heading levels down, as the page that shows it will.

examples.name: OpenInPanel
examples.title: Open links in a panel
examples.description: `renderLink` opens document links in a panel with a plain click, and leaves modified clicks and other links to the browser.

examples.name: CustomElements
examples.title: Render an element your way
examples.description: `components` replaces how an element renders: here a quote becomes an Alert.

examples.name: LinkPicker
examples.title: An application's link picker
examples.description: `onRequestLink` lets the application choose the link, here after a pause that stands in for its picker, with a shorter toolbar.

components.name: Code
components.summary: Inline code in text, highlighted code blocks with a copy button, and the changes between two versions of a file.
useWhen: Text names a command, a value, a file or an identifier, such as `npm run build` (Code).
Source, commands or output of several lines are shown to read or copy, such as an install step (CodeBlock).
People review the changes between two versions of a file, such as a draft against its saved version (CodeDiff).

avoidWhen.text: Keys of a shortcut.
Formatted text written in Markdown, such as notes or a description.
Text people edit, such as a configuration in a form.
The size of a change without its lines.

examples.name: InstallSteps
examples.title: Code
examples.description: Inline code in text, highlighted code blocks with a copy button, and the changes between two versions of a file.

examples.name: HighlightedSource
examples.title: Highlighted source
examples.description: `language` highlights the source, and the label names the file. Copying writes the original string.

examples.name: WrapLongLines
examples.title: Wrap long lines
examples.description: With `wrap` long lines wrap inside the block; copying keeps their original line breaks.

examples.name: PlainOutput
examples.title: Plain text
examples.description: Without a language, such as for a command's output, the source stays plain text.

examples.name: SettingsDiff
examples.title: Code diff
examples.description: CodeDiff shows what a draft changes in a file, and countDiffLines counts its lines for a DiffStat beside the title.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: Small static pills that name a state in its tone or a piece of metadata, show a count, or the size of a change.
useWhen: A short state sits beside the content it describes, such as In review, Blocked or Archived.
A short name or category marks an item, such as a team or a folder (`variant="outline"`).
A piece of neutral metadata sits beside related content, such as a plan or a count of seats.
A number belongs to a label, such as unread messages beside a navigation item or comments on a button (CounterBadge).
The size of a change shows beside a file or a version, such as +12 −3 (DiffStat).

avoidWhen.text: An action, or a choice people turn on and off, even when it looks like a pill.
Choosing one of a few filters or views.
A message about a page or section that needs a sentence.
How full or complete something is, such as storage used.
A headline number with its label and trend, such as on a dashboard.

examples.name: ProjectStatus
examples.title: Badge
examples.description: Small static pills that name a state in its tone or a piece of metadata, show a count, or the size of a change.

examples.name: Tones
examples.title: Tones
examples.description: Each tone carries a meaning; the word says it too.

examples.name: Emphasis
examples.title: Emphasis
examples.description: Soft badges suit most states; a solid badge stands out for the one state that must, and outline badges mark names and categories.

examples.name: NeutralMetadata
examples.title: Neutral metadata
examples.description: A neutral badge holds a fact about the content beside it, such as the plan a card describes or its seats, in place of 0.x's InfoChip.

examples.name: WithIcon
examples.title: With an icon
examples.description: A decorative icon before the label repeats the state at a glance.

examples.name: NavigationCounts
examples.title: Counts in navigation
examples.description: A CounterBadge as a NavList.Item's `end` content, with an `aria-label` that says what it counts; the accent tone marks the count that needs attention.

examples.name: CountsInButtons
examples.title: Counts in buttons
examples.description: In a button, a CounterBadge keeps its own pill and a DiffStat sits on a pill toward the canvas; on a primary button they take the button's text color as an outlined pill.

examples.name: ChangeSize
examples.title: The size of a change
examples.description: DiffStat beside each changed file, read as "124 added lines and 37 removed lines".

components.name: Table
components.summary: Semantic data tables on a rounded surface: sorting, resizable columns, selected rows and stacked rows in narrow containers.
useWhen: People compare values across rows and columns, such as invoices by client, date and amount.
People scan, sort or select records that share the same fields, such as files, orders or members.
Figures read best side by side with their totals, such as hours and amounts per invoice.

avoidWhen.text: A few items, each with its own actions, that people don't compare field by field.
A handful of key figures for a dashboard, such as revenue this month.
Items nested inside other items, such as folders and files.
Arranging content in columns for layout, such as a set of summaries.
A spreadsheet that people edit cell by cell and move through with the arrow keys.

examples.name: ProjectStatus
examples.title: Table
examples.description: Semantic data tables on a rounded surface: sorting, resizable columns, selected rows and stacked rows in narrow containers.

examples.name: NumericColumns
examples.title: Numbers and totals
examples.description: `numeric` cells use tabular figures aligned to the end, so amounts compare down the column. A header cell with `scope="row"` heads the totals row.

examples.name: SortableColumns
examples.title: Sort by a column
examples.description: A header with `onSortChange` becomes a sort button. The application keeps the order, sorts the rows and gives each sortable header its `sortDirection`.

examples.name: SelectRows
examples.title: Select rows
examples.description: A Checkbox in the first cell selects the row; `selected` reports it and takes the selection colors. Every row gets `selected`, `true` or `false`.

examples.name: RowDensity
examples.title: Row density
examples.description: `density` changes only the rows' padding, from `xs` to `lg`; the text stays the same. Buttons in the cells take the small control height at every density.

examples.name: StickyHeader
examples.title: Sticky header
examples.description: The header row stays in view while the rows scroll beneath it. The region needs a height, here from the layout around it.

examples.name: ResizableColumns
examples.title: Resizable columns
examples.description: Drag the boundary at the end of a header, or focus it and press <kbd>←</kbd> or <kbd>→</kbd>; double-click it to restore the starting widths. A name too long for its column ends with an ellipsis.

examples.name: StackedRows
examples.title: Stack rows in a narrow container
examples.description: In a region narrower than `stackBelow`, each row becomes a block titled by its first cell, with the other cells' labels beside their values.

examples.name: SortWhileStacked
examples.title: Sort while rows stack
examples.description: The header row is hidden while rows stack, so `onStackedChange` shows a Select for the order meanwhile. The table and the Select share the same sort state.

components.name: DescriptionList
components.summary: The facts about one thing, as labels and their values, beside each other or stacked by the list's own width.
useWhen: A page, card or sidebar shows the facts about one item, such as a project's owner, status and dates.
Settings of one item sit beside their labels, each a small control, such as a visibility Select.

avoidWhen.text: Many items compared by the same fields.
Items people open or act on, one per row.
A form that people fill in and submit.
One headline number with its trend.

examples.name: Facts
examples.title: DescriptionList
examples.description: The facts about one thing, as labels and their values, beside each other or stacked by the list's own width.

examples.name: Stacked
examples.title: Stacked
examples.description: Contact details with long values put each label above its value.

examples.name: WithControls
examples.title: With controls
examples.description: Settings of one item, each a small control beside its label.

components.name: Kbd
components.summary: Key caps that show a key, or keys pressed together joined by plus, in text, hints and menus.
useWhen: Text names a key or a shortcut, such as "Press Ctrl+P to open a document".
A hint lists the keys a list or a popup handles, such as a footer that says which keys move, open and close.

avoidWhen.text: The shortcut of a menu item, which also needs to reach assistive technology.
Key hints in the footer of a quick-open dialog.
Code, a command or a file name in text.
A status or a count beside a label.

examples.name: ShortcutsInText
examples.title: Kbd
examples.description: Key caps that show a key, or keys pressed together joined by plus, in text, hints and menus.

examples.name: KeyHints
examples.title: Key hints
examples.description: A footer that names the keys a list handles, one hint after another.

examples.name: ShortcutSequence
examples.title: A sequence of shortcuts
examples.description: Each step of a sequence is a Kbd of its own, with "then" between them; `keys` is only for keys pressed together.

examples.name: PlatformKeys
examples.title: The reader's platform
examples.description: Apple keyboards name the Command key where others use Ctrl. Pass the keys of the reader's platform; Kbd shows what it is given.

components.name: AnimatedNumber
components.summary: A number in text that rolls to its new value when it changes, so a count updated elsewhere is noticed.
useWhen: A count changes while people make choices elsewhere, such as matching results in a button's label.
A figure follows a setting people change, such as seats left or a price per billing period.

avoidWhen.text: A count that doesn't change while people look at it, which is plain text.
A compact count beside a label, such as unread messages.
A headline figure with its label and trend, such as on a dashboard.
How far a task has come.

examples.name: ShowResults
examples.title: AnimatedNumber
examples.description: A number in text that rolls to its new value when it changes, so a count updated elsewhere is noticed.

examples.name: SeatsLeft
examples.title: Seats left
examples.description: The sentence is a status region, so the new count is announced as people change it.

examples.name: CustomFormat
examples.title: A formatted value
examples.description: `format` writes the price as a currency; it rolls up for yearly billing and down for monthly.

components.name: Rating
components.summary: A read-only rating as stars filled in half steps, named once for assistive technology.
useWhen: Showing a rating people gave, such as a review score or the average of many reviews.
A compact summary of quality beside a name in a list, a card or a table row.

avoidWhen.text: Asking someone to give a rating; offer a few labelled choices instead.
Asking for a value on a continuous scale, such as a satisfaction score from 0 to 100.
A measurement within a known range, such as storage used.
A key figure on a dashboard, such as the average score this month.
A state or a category, such as Approved or Featured.

examples.name: ReviewScore
examples.title: Rating
examples.description: A read-only rating as stars filled in half steps, named once for assistive technology.

examples.name: Scales
examples.title: Half stars and other scales
examples.description: The stars fill to the value in half steps. `max` sets another scale, such as ten stars.

examples.name: ReviewList
examples.title: A list of reviews
examples.description: In a list of individual reviews the stars are enough; the reviewer's name says whose rating it is.

examples.name: TranslatedLabel
examples.title: The name in another language
examples.description: EnvUIProvider's locale writes the number, here in German with its decimal comma, and `messages.rating.label` the accessible name.

components.name: RelativeTime
components.summary: A moment as text relative to now, such as 3 hours ago, kept current, with the date and time in a tooltip.
useWhen: How long ago or how soon matters more than the exact moment, such as when a report changed or when a review is due.
Activity and lists where times update while the page stays open, such as Draft saved 2 minutes ago.
A string that says how long ago, for a place that takes only text, such as an option label or an accessible name (formatRelativeTime).

avoidWhen.text: A moment people must read exactly, such as a deadline, an appointment or the date of a record; format the date with Intl.DateTimeFormat.
Choosing a date, or a date and time.
Days shown on a month grid.
A count that changes in place, such as seats left.

examples.name: DraftSaved
examples.title: RelativeTime
examples.description: A moment as text relative to now, such as 3 hours ago, kept current, with the date and time in a tooltip.

examples.name: PastAndComing
examples.title: Past and coming moments
examples.description: Past moments read "ago" and coming ones "in"; the unit grows with the distance, from minutes to years.

examples.name: Formats
examples.title: Formats
examples.description: `short` and `narrow` shorten the words for tight spaces.

examples.name: Languages
examples.title: Other languages
examples.description: `locale` writes the text, and the date in the tooltip, in another language.

examples.name: ExactDateNearby
examples.title: The exact date nearby
examples.description: Where the date shows beside it, the relative time needs no tooltip.

examples.name: VersionLabels
examples.title: Text for an option label
examples.description: `formatRelativeTime` returns the same text as a string, for places that take only text. The string doesn't update by itself.

components.name: Disclosure
components.summary: A one-line summary that shows and hides optional details below it, on the native details element.
useWhen: Optional guidance or details that most people don't need, such as how a setting works.
Settings that most people leave alone, such as advanced options in a form.
A list of questions whose answers people open one at a time.

avoidWhen.text: Instructions or errors people need to complete a task, which must stay visible.
Switching between views of the same content.
A hierarchy people expand level by level, such as folders.
Details beside a control that close when people move on.

examples.name: VisibilityHelp
examples.title: Disclosure
examples.description: A one-line summary that shows and hides optional details below it, on the native details element.

examples.name: FrequentQuestions
examples.title: Questions, one open at a time
examples.description: Disclosures with the same `name` act as one group: opening an answer closes the one that was open.

examples.name: OpenOnError
examples.title: Open on an error
examples.description: Advanced settings stay closed until a field in them has an error; `open` and `onOpenChange` then open the disclosure so the error shows.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A round picture of a person or organization, with the default person picture or initials as fallback, as a button, or overlapping in a group.
useWhen: A person or an organization is pictured beside their name, such as in a list of members or a comment.
The signed-in account opens its menu from a picture in the application's chrome (AvatarButton).
Who is involved matters more than each name where space is short, such as a project's members in a row (AvatarGroup).

avoidWhen.text: A status or a count beside a label.
An icon for a thing or an action, not a person.
Every name of a list of people that should be read.

examples.name: PersonWithName
examples.title: Avatar
examples.description: A round picture of a person or organization, with the default person picture or initials as fallback, as a button, or overlapping in a group.

examples.name: Sizes
examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: Four sizes, from a compact row to a profile page; each is labelled here, with no name beside it.

examples.name: Fallbacks
examples.title: Pictures and fallbacks
examples.description: A picture covers the circle. One that fails to load shows the default person picture, and an organization shows its initials.

examples.name: AccountButton
examples.title: Account menu
examples.description: AvatarButton opens the account menu; its tooltip shows the name and the e-mail address, and its halo stays while the menu is open.

examples.name: ProjectMembers
examples.title: Members in a row
examples.description: Groups on List rows show three or two avatars and count the rest, also people who are counted in `total` but not passed. The ring takes the row's fill.

examples.name: PressableAvatars
examples.title: Pressable avatars
examples.description: With `onPersonClick` every avatar is a button named after the person; a person with `href` is a link. The chip lists the people it hides.

components.name: Message
components.summary: Conversation entries in a log: compact bubbles for your own messages, full-width content from others.
useWhen: A conversation between the person using the app and others, such as a chat with a person or an assistant.
A thread of comments in the order they were written, each with its author and time.
A reply that streams in or messages that load while people read, which assistive technology should announce politely.

avoidWhen.text: The field where people write and send the next message.
Items people scan, open and act on, such as a list of conversations.
A short notification that comes and goes, such as Message sent.
A message about a page or a section, such as a warning before a form.
Formatted text on its own, outside a conversation.

examples.name: Conversation
examples.title: Message
examples.description: Conversation entries in a log: compact bubbles for your own messages, full-width content from others.

examples.name: DeliveryStatus
examples.title: Delivery status
examples.description: A message that couldn't be sent says so and offers Retry; while it is sent again it shows Sending.

examples.name: FormattedAnswer
examples.title: A formatted answer
examples.description: Markdown inside a message from someone else keeps the full width. A CopyButton in `actions` copies the answer.

examples.name: CommentThread
examples.title: A comment thread
examples.description: Comments by several people read best at full width: each is `from="other"`, with its author and a RelativeTime in the header.

components.name: Stat
components.summary: Labelled key figures for dashboards, with how they changed and over what period, grouped in even columns.
useWhen: The few figures that sum up a view, such as a dashboard's active projects, tasks done and lead time.
A figure with how it changed since an earlier period, such as +12% from last month.

avoidWhen.text: Many values to compare or sort, such as figures for each project.
A quantity within a known range, such as the seats assigned of a plan's five.
A count on a control, such as unread messages on a tab.
A summary people open or act on, with a description and actions.

examples.name: ProjectHealth
examples.title: Stat
examples.description: Labelled key figures for dashboards, with how they changed and over what period, grouped in even columns.

examples.name: TrendTones
examples.title: Good news and bad news
examples.description: Fewer risks take the success tone, a higher error rate the danger tone, and a rising cost that stays within budget the warning tone.

examples.name: OnAPane
examples.title: On a pane
examples.description: On a pane, the group takes the muted background and a smaller padding; the heading names the group.

examples.name: InACard
examples.title: One figure in a card
examples.description: A stat on its own has no surface; a Card gives it one.

components.name: CalendarHeatmap
components.summary: A calendar grid that shades each day by its value, with a tooltip and keyboard access for every day.
useWhen: A count per day over weeks or months shows a pattern, such as activity or deployments, where the pattern matters more than each number.

avoidWhen.text: Exact figures people compare or read one by one.
A headline number with its trend.
Choosing a day.
A share of a known range, such as storage used.

examples.name: Deployments
examples.title: CalendarHeatmap
examples.description: A calendar grid that shades each day by its value, with a tooltip and keyboard access for every day.

examples.name: ColorByRank
examples.title: Color by rank
examples.description: `thresholds` from quantiles of the active days make each step hold about as many days, so a few very busy days don't leave the rest pale.

examples.name: Localized
examples.title: In another language
examples.description: EnvUIProvider's locale names the months, weekdays and dates in German, and its messages translate the legend; weeks start on Monday.
