props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether a dialog the application doesn't control is open on the first render.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the requested state, and why, when the dialog asks to open or close: from the trigger, Escape, an outside press, the close button or a DialogClose. Not called for a dismissal that pending blocks.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element that opens the dialog, such as a Button. It reports the dialog it opens, and focus returns to it on close. Omit it for a dialog the application opens with open.

props.name: title
props.description: The dialog's heading and accessible name, such as “Delete project?”.

props.name: description
props.description: Muted text under the title that describes the dialog to assistive technology too, such as what its action changes.

props.name: children
props.description: The content between the heading and the actions, such as text, fields or a list.

props.name: actions
props.description: The dialog's own actions, after the built-in close button, with the primary action last. They close the dialog only where they are DialogClose or set open to false.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The label of the built-in close button that starts the actions, such as Cancel.

props.name: placement
props.description: center for a modal in the middle of the window; top for a modal near the top of the window for search-like tasks, so results grow downward without moving the field. For a panel at an edge of the window, use Drawer.

props.name: width
props.description: md, 28 rem wide, or lg, 44 rem, for content-heavy dialogs such as tables, comparisons and longer forms. Both narrow to fit the window.

props.name: modal
props.description: true traps focus in the dialog over a backdrop, hides the page from assistive technology, blocks presses on it and locks its scroll. false leaves the page usable beside the dialog; it then closes when focus or a press goes outside it, unless disablePointerDismissal.

props.name: disablePointerDismissal
props.description: Keep the dialog open on presses outside it, and a non-modal dialog also when focus moves outside. Escape and the close buttons still close it.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: The element to focus when the dialog opens, as a ref or a function of how it was opened. By default focus moves to the first focusable element inside, such as the first field, or to the dialog itself when opened by touch.

props.name: finalFocus
props.description: The element to focus when the dialog closes, such as the row that opened it. By default focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus when the dialog opened.

props.name: pending
props.description: Work started from the dialog is in progress. Escape, outside presses and the close buttons cannot dismiss it until pending returns to false. The built-in close button is disabled and the dialog reports busy; a DialogClose stays enabled and runs its onClick, so disable it too. Set pending on the action that started the work as well.

DialogClose.description: A button inside a Dialog or a Drawer that closes it after its own onClick, for an action other than the built-in close button, such as Don't save or Done. It takes Button's props and is secondary by default.

props.name: variant
props.description: The emphasis: primary for the main action of a view, secondary and outline for the rest, ghost for an application's chrome, such as a toolbar, and text for a link-like action. Without it, the button takes the variant its container gives where that variant takes its tone, such as ghost in a toolbar, and else primary.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning: neutral for most actions; accent, on a primary button only, for a rare consequential action, with 0.5 rem corners; danger for an action that deletes or ends something. Secondary buttons are always neutral.

props.name: underline
props.description: Show an underline for the text variant; defaults to false.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale, such as sm for an action in a table cell or lg for the main call to action of a page. Without it, the button takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another. A button beside a field takes the field's size.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the width of the container, such as the actions of a narrow form stacked in a column. An icon-only button keeps its square size.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as an Add icon.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: A decorative icon after the label, such as a ChevronRight for a next step.

props.name: pending
props.description: Work started by this button is running: a spinner replaces the content without changing the button's size, and the button reports busy and ignores activation until pending ends.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The action's name, such as Delete draft, for an icon-only button.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Show only icon, in a square button that keeps its size; name it with aria-label.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon of an icon-only button.

DiffStat.description: The size of a change as one compact pill, such as +12 −3: additions in the success tone and deletions in the danger tone, on a counter badge's quiet fill.

props.name: additions
props.description: Lines or items added, shown as +12 in the success tone, in the locale's digits.

props.name: deletions
props.description: Lines or items removed, shown as −3 in the danger tone, in the locale's digits.

props.name: formatLabel
props.description: Full meaning for assistive technology. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.diffStat.label`.

Disclosure.description: A summary that shows and hides the details below it, on the native details element.

props.name: title
props.description: The summary: one line that says what the details hold and opens or closes them.

props.name: children
props.description: The details, shown below the summary while the disclosure is open.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the details show, for a controlled disclosure: update it from onOpenChange. Use defaultOpen instead to leave it to the disclosure.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the details show at first, for a disclosure that keeps its own state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Receives whether the details show, each time the disclosure opens or closes.

DocumentTabs.description: Editor-style closable tabs for open documents; the application renders the active document.

props.name: items
props.description: The open documents, in tab order.

props.name: value
props.description: The active tab, or null.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when a tab is clicked or reached with the arrow keys, Home or End.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called from a tab's close button, a middle click, Delete or Backspace on the focused tab, and Close in the tab's context menu.

props.name: onPin
props.description: Called when a tab is double-clicked, typically to keep a preview tab open.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the tab strip.

props.name: panelId
props.description: Id of the panel the application renders for the active tab.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The name of the context menu's item that closes a tab, and the tooltip of its close button.

props.name: onCloseAll
props.description: Called from Close all tabs in the context menu. Each tab opens a context menu that closes it on right click, long press, the Menu key and Shift+F10; with onCloseAll, the menu also offers Close all tabs, and the strip around the tabs opens it too.

props.name: closeAllLabel
props.description: Label of the Close all tabs item.

props.name: contextMenuLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the context menu.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the strip, the tab list.

props.name: style
props.description: The strip's inline style.

props.name: ref
props.description: The strip, the tab list element.

Drawer.description: A panel that slides in from the start or end edge of the window over the page, for filters, details, an inspector or a phone's navigation: a modal by default, which traps focus and returns it on close, or beside the page with modal false. It takes the whole width of a narrow window, and a swipe toward its edge closes it. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the drawer's surface.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the drawer is open, for a drawer the application controls with onOpenChange.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether a drawer the application doesn't control is open on the first render.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the requested state, and why, when the drawer asks to open or close: from the trigger, Escape, an outside press, the close button, a swipe toward its edge or a DialogClose. Not called for a dismissal that pending blocks.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element that opens the drawer, such as a Button. It reports the drawer it opens, and focus returns to it on close. Omit it for a drawer the application opens with open.

props.name: side
props.description: The edge of the window the drawer slides in from: start, the left in left-to-right text, or end, the right. It follows the text direction, so it is mirrored in right-to-left text.

props.name: title
props.description: The drawer's heading and accessible name, such as Filters. Without one, name the drawer with aria-label, as a navigation drawer does.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The drawer's accessible name where it has no visible title.

props.name: description
props.description: Muted text under the title that describes the drawer to assistive technology too.

props.name: children
props.description: The content under the heading, such as filters, details or navigation. It scrolls.

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions at the end of the content, such as Apply, with the primary action last.

props.name: closeButton
props.description: Whether the drawer shows its close button, a CloseButton at the end of the heading. Leave it out only where the drawer holds a control that closes it, such as a sidebar's own toggle.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name.

props.name: width
props.description: md, 24 rem, for details and filters; lg, 44 rem, for content-heavy panels such as tables and comparisons; or any CSS length, such as min(20rem, 100vw - 2rem). md and lg take the whole width of a window too narrow to leave the page beside them.

props.name: modal
props.description: true traps focus in the drawer over a backdrop, hides the page from assistive technology, blocks presses on it and locks its scroll. false leaves the page usable beside the drawer, for an inspector; it then closes when focus or a press goes outside it, unless disablePointerDismissal.

props.name: disablePointerDismissal
props.description: Keep the drawer open on presses outside it, and a non-modal drawer also when focus moves outside, such as an inspector beside the page it inspects. Escape and the close buttons still close it.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: The element to focus when the drawer opens, as a ref or a function of how it was opened. By default focus moves to the first element inside that takes Tab, such as the close button, or to the drawer itself when opened by touch or when nothing inside takes focus.

props.name: finalFocus
props.description: The element to focus when the drawer closes, as a ref or a function of how it closed, such as the main content after a navigation. By default focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus when it opened.

props.name: pending
props.description: Work started from the drawer is in progress: Escape, outside presses, swipes and the close button cannot dismiss it until pending returns to false, and the drawer reports busy.

DropZone.description: A drop target for files that also opens the file picker; the application shows what was chosen.

props.name: label
props.description: What to drop or choose, such as "Drop a logo here, or browse". With the description, it names the zone, as its visible text does.

props.name: description
props.description: Which files fit, such as "PNG, JPG or WebP up to 2 MB"; it is read as part of the name.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replaces the upload icon.

props.name: accept
props.description: The file types the zone takes, as in the native accept attribute: MIME types such as image/png, groups such as image/*, and extensions such as .webp. Any file by default.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Take several files at once; otherwise the zone takes the first file.

props.name: onDropAccepted
props.description: Receives the dropped or chosen files that the zone takes.

props.name: onDropRejected
props.description: Receives the files that do not match accept, and those after the first without multiple.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The zone can't be pressed or focused and takes no files; it still keeps the browser from opening dropped files.

props.name: pending
props.description: The application is working on the files: a spinner replaces the icon, the zone reports that it is busy and takes no new files.

props.name: error
props.description: A message linked to the zone, whose outline takes the error color.

props.name: size
props.description: md is the tall area with a large icon; sm is one row with a small icon, for a form or a sidebar.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits files with a native form under this name: the last files the zone took, until the form resets, or files.

props.name: files
props.description: The files a named zone submits when the application keeps them, such as after a Remove action; they replace the files the zone took, also after the form resets.

props.name: form
props.description: The id of a form the zone belongs to when it is outside of it.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: The native file input that opens the file picker, for example from a Replace button.

EmptyState.description: What a region shows when it has nothing to show: no items yet, no matches, or content that failed to load. A title, a description, an optional icon and the action that resolves the state.

props.name: title
props.description: What is missing or what happened, such as "No projects yet"; a heading of `headingLevel`.

props.name: description
props.description: Why, and what people can do, in a sentence or two of muted text under the title.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon above the text; an error state shows the error icon without it.

props.name: action
props.description: The action that resolves the state, such as a Button that creates the first item.

props.name: children
props.description: More content under the description, such as a short list of next steps.

props.name: tone
props.description: neutral for a state with nothing to show yet; danger for content that failed to load, which shows the error icon by default and is announced as an alert. Pair it with a retry action.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The title's heading level in the page outline; 4 by default. The appearance stays the same.

props.name: align
props.description: `start` (default) for a state inside a card, panel or dialog. `center` for a state that takes the place of a page's or region's content: a larger icon, centred text and action, centred vertically in the height the application gives it.

EnvUIProvider.description: Sets the locale, the strings and the text direction of the envUI components inside it. envUI works without it, in English, in the runtime's locale and in each element's direction; an application that translates or formats for its people wraps itself, or a region, in one.

props.name: locale
props.description: The BCP 47 locale envUI formats numbers, dates and relative times in, and reads plural rules, collation and the week's first day from, such as de-CH. Without it, the runtime's locale, from the browser once the page has hydrated.

props.name: messages
props.description: Overrides of envUI's built-in English strings, per namespace, such as `{ common: { close: 'Schließen' }, toast: { hidden: ({ count }) => t('hidden', { count }) } }`. A message is a string, or a function of the values it names. Nested providers merge per namespace, the inner winning; a component's own label prop, such as closeLabel, wins over both.

props.name: dir
props.description: The text direction for keyboard and placement logic, such as which arrow key moves forward and which side a popup's start is. Without it, each component reads the direction at its element, from dir attributes and CSS. It doesn't set the dir attribute: set that on the page or region.

Field.Control.description: The control: a native text input in the outlined field look by default, or any control through render, such as render={<MyControl />}, which receives the control's props, id and ref. A custom control styles itself; the class env-field-control gives it the field's outline.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback fired when the `value` changes. Use when controlled.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the control height of the container.

Field.Description.description: Lasting guidance under the control, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

Field.Error.description: A message under the control that says how to correct the value, with an error icon. It shows while the field is invalid, from its own validation or from invalid on Field.Root, and is linked to the control; match="valueMissing" and the like show it for one kind of failure, and match={true} always.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: match
props.description: Determines whether to show the error message according to the field's [ValidityState](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ValidityState). Specifying `true` will always show the error message, and lets external libraries control the visibility.

props.name: children
props.description: How to correct the value. Without children, the browser's validation message shows.

Field.Label.description: The field's visible name; it names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: nativeLabel
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<label>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a label (for example, `<div>`). This is useful to avoid inheriting label behaviors on `<button>` controls (such as `<Select.Trigger>` and `<Combobox.Trigger>`), including avoiding `:hover` on the button when hovering the label, and preventing clicks on the label from firing on the button.

Field.Root.description: A labelled form control with its description and error, for a control envUI has no field for, such as a control of the application's own: Field.Label names Field.Control, and the description and the error describe it, with ids, aria-invalid and the disabled state wired through Base UI's Field.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction. Takes precedence over the `disabled` prop on the `<Field.Control>` component.

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted. Takes precedence over the `name` prop on the `<Field.Control>` component.

props.name: validate
props.type: ((value: unknown, formValues: Form.Values) => string | string[] | null | void | Promise<string | string[] | null | void>) | undefined
props.description: A function for custom validation. Return a string or an array of strings with the error message(s) if the value is invalid. Returning nothing, `null`, an empty string, or an empty array means the value is valid. Asynchronous functions are supported, but they do not prevent form submission when using `validationMode="onSubmit"`.

props.name: validationMode
props.description: Determines when the field should be validated. This takes precedence over the `validationMode` prop on `<Form>`. - `onSubmit`: triggers validation when the form is submitted, and re-validates on change after submission. - `onBlur`: triggers validation when the control loses focus. - `onChange`: triggers validation on every change to the control value.

props.name: validationDebounceTime
props.description: How long to wait between `validate` callbacks if `validationMode="onChange"` is used. Specified in milliseconds.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Whether the field is invalid. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: dirty
props.description: Whether the field's value has been changed from its initial value. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: touched
props.description: Whether the field has been touched. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description: A ref to imperative actions. - `validate`: Validates the field when called.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

HoverCard.description: Supplementary details that open beside their trigger on hover and keyboard focus, like a link preview. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the card.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element that opens the card on hover and keyboard focus; it receives the ref.

props.name: children
props.description: The details. Supplementary: never the only place essential information appears.

props.name: side
props.description: bottom, top, left or right, or inline-start and inline-end, which follow the text direction.

props.name: align
props.description: Lines the card up with the trigger's centre, start or end along the side.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds the pointer rests on the trigger before the card opens; focus opens it at once.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: Milliseconds before it closes once the pointer leaves the trigger and the card.

props.name: width
props.description: md about 20 rem wide; lg about 28 rem.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the card shows; with `onOpenChange` it controls the card.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled card starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new state, and why, when hover, focus or Esc opens or closes the card.

Icon.description: Shared SVG defaults; custom icons may supply their own viewBox and children.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for a meaningful standalone icon. Omit for decoration.

IconButton.description: Shorthand for Button's icon-only mode. Without a variant it takes its container's, and else the neutral secondary one.

props.name: variant
props.description: The emphasis, as Button's. Without it, the button takes the variant its container gives, such as ghost in a toolbar, and else secondary.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning, as Button's: accent on a primary button only, and danger on a primary, outline, ghost or text one. A secondary button is always neutral.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon, such as Settings.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The action's name, which assistive technology announces, such as Open settings.

props.name: pending
props.description: As Button's: a spinner replaces the icon while the work runs.

props.name: size
props.description: As Button's: the height, and the width, of the square button.

Kbd.description: A keyboard key, or a combination of keys with keys.

props.name: keys
props.description: Keys pressed together, such as ['Ctrl', 'P']: one key cap each, joined by +, inside an outer `<kbd>`. Without it, the children are one key.

Link.description: A destination inside running text, underlined by default. It is a native link, through the LinkProvider's link component, in the text button's colors.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: the element is a native link, through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: disabled
props.description: A disabled button cannot be pressed; a disabled link has no destination, cannot be focused or followed, and reports aria-disabled.

props.name: underline
props.description: Underline the link; true by default, so it stands out from the text around it.

LinkProvider.description: Connects envUI links to the application's router without a router dependency in envUI.

props.name: component
props.description: Renders every envUI destination (Button, Link, NavList.Item, Card, Pager links and menu links with href). It must render an anchor and forward native props and ref, for example a router's link that navigates on the client.

List.Item.description: One `li` row with a label, a description and an action; the current row, content at its start, and in a reorderable list a drag handle. It renders on the server: only the handle of a reorderable row needs the browser.

props.name: label
props.description: The row's main text, such as an item's name; a link marked `data-row-target` in an interactive row.

props.name: description
props.description: A short fact in muted text below the label, such as who changed the item and when.

props.name: action
props.description: A control at the end of the row, such as a Button; it moves below the text when it doesn't fit.

props.name: children
props.description: More content after the label and the description, such as a Badge.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The row opens something through a link or button inside: it reacts to hover, keyboard focus inside it and presses. Mark that link or button `data-row-target` to stretch it over the row.

props.name: selected
props.description: The current row, such as the one whose details show beside a list: the selected fill, and `aria-current="true"` on its `data-row-target` element in the label, description or children, or on the row without one.

props.name: start
props.description: Content before the label, such as an Avatar, an icon or a Checkbox for choosing several rows; a row whose checkbox is checked takes the selected fill.

props.name: textValue
props.description: The row's label as plain text, for its drag handle's name and the reorder announcements where `label` isn't a string.

List.Root.description: A `ul` of connected rows with shared outer corners. In a muted Surface that holds only lists, such as `<Surface background="muted" padding={3}>`, the rows take the raised fill, so they stand out from it. With onReorder, people move the rows by their handles.

props.name: density
props.description: How tightly the rows pack: xs, sm, md or lg changes only their block padding, never the text.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: Makes the rows reorderable: each row gets a drag handle at its start, moved by dragging it, by pressing it or by keyboard, and the list calls this with the row's index and the index it is dropped at. The application moves the item in its own state; nothing moves until it does. The rows are the list's children, directly or in arrays and fragments: List.Item elements, or elements of a row component that passes the props it doesn't use on to its List.Item, such as `function SlideRow({ slide, ...props }) { return <List.Item {...props} label={slide} />; }`.

ListDetail.Detail.description: The detail pane, after the handle that resizes the list. Stacked, it shows only while detailShown, with a back button to the list at its start.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the detail's region, such as the chosen item's name.

ListDetail.List.description: The list pane, a region named by its label. Stacked, it hides while the detail shows.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list's region, such as Projects.

ListDetail.Root.description: A list beside the detail of its chosen item, on SplitPane, with the list's width resizable. Below `stackBelow` of its own width it shows one at a time: the list, or the detail with a back button, which moves focus between them.

props.name: detailShown
props.description: Whether the detail is what people are looking at, such as after choosing an item. A stacked layout shows the detail instead of the list while it is true; side by side, both show.

props.name: onBack
props.description: Called by the back button of a stacked detail; set detailShown to false in it.

props.name: backLabel
props.description: The back button's label, which names where it goes, such as All projects. It depends on the content, so there is no default.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: A width, such as '44rem', or a number of pixels: while the layout itself is narrower, it shows the list or the detail, one at a time.

props.name: defaultListSize
props.description: The list's share of the width in percent until people resize it.

props.name: minListSize
props.description: The list's smallest share of the width in percent.

props.name: maxListSize
props.description: The list's largest share of the width in percent.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: The name of the handle that resizes the list, such as Resize project list.

props.name: persist
props.description: Keeps the list's width under this localStorage key.

props.name: children
props.description: The list and the detail: ListDetail.List, then ListDetail.Detail.

LoadingState.description: A region of placeholders for content that is loading, such as Skeletons in the shape of a card: a status named by label and marked busy, which stacks its children 0.5 rem apart.

props.name: label
props.description: What is loading, such as Loading project, which names the region for assistive technology; an aria-label overrides it.

Markdown.description: CommonMark prose with tables, task lists and other extensions, in envUI typography and code.

props.name: children
props.description: The Markdown string to render.

props.name: headingOffset
props.description: Add to the document's heading levels; levels are capped at h6.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: Receives safe hrefs and native anchor props. Retain a real anchor destination.

props.name: codeCopyable
props.description: Gives each code block a copy button; false by default.

props.name: components
props.description: react-markdown component overrides, merged over envUI's own; the application's win. Native props such as id and className reach the element.

props.name: remarkPlugins
props.description: remark plugins that run after envUI's own Markdown extensions.

props.name: rehypePlugins
props.description: rehype plugins, such as heading ids; envUI adds none of its own.

MarkdownEditor.description: Native Markdown source editing, shared formatting history, and optional preview.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: Formatting actions; false hides the toolbar. Undo/redo accompany a visible toolbar.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The source an uncontrolled editor starts with, and that a form reset restores.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-text-field.

props.name: value
props.description: The Markdown source of a controlled editor; replacing it clears the undo history.

props.name: rows
props.description: The lines the field shows: with fixed sizing, its height in rows, at least 7.5 rem; with content sizing, the lines it starts at and shrinks back to, also under 7.5 rem. Without rows, both start at 7.5 rem.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the whole source after typing, formatting, undo or redo.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look, as TextField's: outline, underline or ghost. A text area is always tall, with its label resting at the top, so it has no floating variant.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: sizing
props.description: How the height follows the text: fixed keeps its height, scrolls and resizes from the bottom edge, by dragging it or with the arrow keys; content grows and shrinks with the text.

props.name: preview
props.description: Show Write/Preview tabs. Preview uses the same public Markdown renderer.

props.name: previewProps
props.description: Options of the Markdown that renders the preview: headingOffset, renderLink and codeCopyable.

props.name: onRequestLink
props.description: Optional application picker. Return null to cancel; otherwise return an ordinary link.

Menu.CheckboxItem.description: An independent on/off option; a check mark shows while it is on.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the option is on; a check mark shows while it is.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Called with the new state when the item is toggled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The item stays in place, dimmed, but cannot be toggled.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Close the menu after toggling; off by default, so several options can change.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the item's row.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as Settings.

props.name: children
props.description: The item's label, which names it.

props.name: description
props.description: A second, muted line; announced as the item's description.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: Keyboard hint at the end, such as Ctrl+P, shown as Kbd keys and announced as aria-keyshortcuts; a sequence, such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S, shows its keys without the attribute. The application handles the shortcut itself.

props.name: end
props.description: End content, such as a Badge or CounterBadge; it is part of the item's name.

Menu.Group.description: A labelled group of related items, with a small heading above its rows.

props.name: label
props.description: Small heading that names the group for assistive technology too.

props.name: children
props.description: Items of the group.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the group.

Menu.Header.description: Non-interactive context at the top of a menu, such as the signed-in account.

props.name: children
props.description: The context, such as the signed-in person's avatar, name and e-mail address.

Menu.Item.description: One action (onClick) or destination (href) in a Menu. Destinations use the LinkProvider's link and close the menu as they are followed.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The item is unavailable: it stays in place, dimmed, and reports aria-disabled; its action does not run, and a destination has no link to follow.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the item's row.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as Settings.

props.name: children
props.description: The item's label, which names it.

props.name: description
props.description: A second, muted line; announced as the item's description.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: Keyboard hint at the end, such as Ctrl+P, shown as Kbd keys and announced as aria-keyshortcuts; a sequence, such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S, shows its keys without the attribute. The application handles the shortcut itself.

props.name: end
props.description: End content, such as a Badge or CounterBadge; it is part of the item's name.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: the item is a link, through the LinkProvider's link component, and the menu closes as it is followed.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Runs as the destination is followed, before the menu closes, such as to record the choice; the link still navigates.

props.name: target
props.description: Where the destination opens, such as _blank, as on a native link.

props.name: rel
props.description: The destination's relationship to the page, such as noopener, as on a native link.

Menu.RadioGroup.description: One choice among several items; the checked item shows a check mark.

props.name: value
props.description: Value of the checked item, or null for none.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the chosen item's value.

props.name: children
props.description: Menu.RadioItem elements.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional heading; the group is then labelled like Menu.Group.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of a heading elsewhere in the menu that names the group, in place of label.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the group.

props.name: value
props.description: The value the Menu.RadioGroup reports when this item is chosen.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The item stays in place, dimmed, but cannot be chosen.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Close the menu after choosing.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the item's row.

props.name: children
props.description: The item's label, which names it.

props.name: end
props.description: End content, such as a Badge or CounterBadge; it is part of the item's name.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as Settings.

props.name: description
props.description: A second, muted line; announced as the item's description.

Menu.Root.description: A list of actions and destinations that opens from a trigger; keyboard and focus follow the menu pattern. The popup is raised above the page, with rows of the scale's row height, hairline separators and small keys for shortcuts.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The control that opens the menu, such as a Button or an AvatarButton; it receives the menu button semantics and ref, so it must accept native props and a ref.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the menu, such as Account.

props.name: children
props.description: Menu.Header, Menu.Item, Menu.Group, Menu.RadioGroup, Menu.CheckboxItem, Menu.Submenu and Menu.Separator elements.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of the trigger the menu opens on; it flips to the other side where the window has no room. inline-start and inline-end follow the text direction.

props.name: align
props.description: How the menu lines up with the trigger along that side.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the menu is open, for a controlled menu; leave it out and the menu opens and closes itself.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled menu starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new visibility as the menu opens or closes.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the menu popup. ref, style, data attributes and the other native props go to the popup too; the trigger is the element you pass.

Menu.Submenu.description: A row that opens a nested menu beside it, on hover or with the keyboard. The submenu opens in the theme of its menu, and lines its first row up with the row that opened it.

props.name: label
props.description: The label of the row that opens the submenu, which names the row.

props.name: children
props.description: The submenu's items: Menu.Item, Menu.Group, Menu.Separator and the other parts, nested submenus too.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the submenu; by default the label, when it is a string.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The row stays in place, dimmed, but cannot open its submenu.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled visibility; onOpenChange also suits loading the items as the submenu opens.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled submenu starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new visibility as the submenu opens or closes, for example to load its items.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the submenu popup.

props.name: ref
props.description: The submenu popup's ref.

props.name: style
props.description: The submenu popup's inline style.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as Settings.

props.name: description
props.description: A second, muted line; announced as the item's description.

Menubar.Menu.description: One menu of a Menubar.Root: a small text trigger and the menu that opens below it. After a command, focus returns to where it was before the menubar took it, as in a desktop application.

props.name: label
props.description: The trigger's text, such as File.

props.name: accessKey
props.description: A letter of the label, such as F for File. With Menubar.Root's accessKeys, holding Alt underlines it and Alt with the letter opens the menu.

props.name: children
props.description: The menu's items: Menu.Item, Menu.Submenu, Menu.Separator and the other menu parts.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the menu; by default the label, when it is a string.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The trigger stays in place, dimmed, but doesn't open its menu.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled visibility.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled menu starts open; closed by default.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the menu opens or closes, with the element that had focus before the menubar took it.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the menu popup.

props.name: ref
props.description: The menu popup's ref; the trigger is the menubar's own.

props.name: style
props.description: The menu popup's inline style.

Menubar.Root.description: An application menubar: a row of small text buttons that open menus, such as File, Edit, View and Help. Once a menu is open, hovering another trigger or pressing ← and → switches to its menu. Opening a menu neither locks scrolling nor shifts the page.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the menubar, such as Application menu.

props.name: children
props.description: Menubar.Menu elements.

props.name: accessKeys
props.description: Desktop access keys, off by default: holding Alt underlines each menu's accessKey, Alt with that letter opens the menu, and Alt alone moves focus to the menubar and back. Turn it on for one menubar per window.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every menu of the menubar.

Message.description: One entry of a conversation, such as a chat message or a comment, as an article: a compact bubble at the inline end for your own messages, full-width content for others', with an optional author, meta, status and actions.

props.name: from
props.description: self: written by the person using the app, a compact bubble at the inline end. other: from anyone else, such as an assistant or another participant, full-width content without a bubble.

props.name: author
props.description: Who wrote the message, such as a name, shown above it at weight 500. Leave it out where the conversation makes it clear, such as on your own messages in a conversation with one person.

props.name: meta
props.description: Supporting facts beside the author, in the muted color, such as the time or a RelativeTime.

props.name: actions
props.description: Small actions below the message, such as Copy or Retry: buttons without a variant or size of their own are ghost buttons at the small control height, with the touch height on touch screens; at the inline end for your own messages. A text IconButton at the edge lines its icon up with the message. false and null count as absent.

props.name: status
props.description: A message on its way, sending, with a spinner and Sending; or one that could not be sent, failed, with an error icon and Not sent in the danger tone and, on your own message, a red outline around the bubble. Without it the message is sent.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: The text beside the status icon, such as "Could not deliver". It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.message.sending` and `.failed`.

props.name: children
props.description: The message. Plain text keeps its line breaks; formatted content, such as Markdown, fills the width of a message from someone else.

MessageList.description: The messages of a conversation in order, as a log: assistive technology politely announces messages added anywhere in it and text that changes. Set busy while a reply streams in or earlier messages load. Name it with aria-label or aria-labelledby.

props.name: busy
props.description: Messages are still changing, such as a reply streaming in or earlier messages loading. The log reports aria-busy, so assistive technology can wait for the change to finish instead of announcing every step.

Meter.description: A measurement within a known range, such as the seats assigned of a plan or the storage used of a quota: a label, an optional value and a bar, exposed as a meter. For how much of a task is done, use Progress.

props.name: value
props.description: The measurement, between min and max. A value outside the range shows, and is reported, as the nearest end.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar shows, such as Seats assigned; it is visible above the bar and names it.

props.name: min
props.description: The low end of the range.

props.name: max
props.description: The high end of the range.

props.name: valueText
props.description: The value as text at the end of the label's row, formatted by the application, such as 2 of 5 or 40%. Without it, no value shows.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: The value as assistive technology reads it, with its unit in words, such as 2 of 5 seats. Without it, a screen reader reads the value as a percentage of the range, in the locale of the nearest EnvUIProvider.

NavList.Group.description: Related items under a small heading, as an item of NavList.Root with a list of its own.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's visible heading, such as Settings, in small muted text above its items; it also names the group's list for assistive technology.

props.name: children
props.description: The group's NavList.Item elements, each of which renders its own list item.

NavList.Item.description: A navigation destination: a native link with href, through the LinkProvider's link component, or a button that changes the view. It shows an optional icon, its label and end content, marks the current destination with selected, and shows only its icon with iconOnly or inside a compact AppShell sidebar. Inside NavList.Root or NavList.Group it renders its own list item.

props.name: selected
props.description: The item is the current destination or view: it takes the navigation selection fill and label color, fills its Material Symbol, and reports aria-current="page" unless aria-current is set.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The destination is unavailable: dimmed, and left out of the tab order. A disabled button cannot be pressed; a disabled link has no destination and reports aria-disabled. An icon-only item still shows its label on hover.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as one of envUI's Material Symbols, which shows filled while the item is selected and outlined otherwise, also inside a wrapper. Required with iconOnly.

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: The icon shown while the item is selected, for a custom icon without a filled form; Material Symbols need none.

props.name: end
props.description: Content at the end of the item, such as a CounterBadge or a Badge; it is part of the item's accessible name. An icon-only item shows a small accent dot instead. Where the name comes from aria-label, or from the label of an icon-only item, it adds the content: a number, or a CounterBadge without aria-label, as a count from EnvUIProvider's messages.navList.itemCount, such as Inbox, 3 new; a CounterBadge's aria-label, such as Inbox, 4 unread, or other content's text or aria-label, such as Labs, Beta, as it is, through messages.navList.itemEnd.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The destination's name, such as Inbox, for an icon-only item; the tooltip shows it. The item's name adds its end content, such as a count.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: the element is a native link, through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Show only the icon, in a circle as tall as the item, as in a collapsed sidebar; a tooltip at the item's inline end shows aria-label on hover and keyboard focus. Inside a compact AppShell sidebar, items with an icon show only it without this prop.

NavList.Root.description: A plain list of navigation items and groups, for a sidebar or anywhere else. It adds no landmark of its own: place it in a nav element, or in a region that is one, such as AppShell's sidebar. Name it with aria-label or aria-labelledby when the page has more than one.

OrganizationSwitcher.description: Shows the active organization and switches between the person's organizations; fits AppShell's context area.

props.name: items
props.description: Organizations the signed-in person belongs to, in display order.

props.name: value
props.description: The active organization's id, or null before one is chosen.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the id of the organization chosen, unless it is the active one; the application switches and reports progress.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: Offers creating an organization at the end of the menu, or as the only action without organizations.

props.name: heading
props.description: Heading inside the menu.

props.name: createLabel
props.description: Label of the create action.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Trigger text while no organization is active.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Prevents opening, for example while a switch is in progress.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the menu.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the trigger button, or of the create button without organizations.

props.name: ref
props.description: The menu popup's ref; the trigger is a Button of its own.

props.name: style
props.description: The menu popup's inline style.

Page.description: The column a page's content sits in: centered, as wide as `width` at most, with the page gutter at its edges and the page's header at its top. It adds no landmark; put it in AppShell.Main, or the application's own main.

props.name: width
props.description: How wide the content may grow: sm (40 rem) for a form or a settings page, md (60 rem) for a document or a detail page, lg (76 rem) for a dashboard or a list, full for content that uses the whole width, such as a board. The column is centered in the space it has.

props.name: header
props.description: The page's heading, usually a PageHeader, at the top of the same column.

props.name: gutter
props.description: Pads the column at its inline edges with the page gutter, which grows from 1 to 2 rem with the viewport. False leaves the edges to the content, such as a page that is one full-bleed table.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<article />}; a div by default. The page's class and attributes merge into its props.

props.name: children
props.description: The page's content, under its header.

PageHeader.description: The heading of a page: its title with an optional trail above it, a description, leading content, meta beside the title, actions at the end and a toolbar row under it. It responds to its own width, and can stick to the top of the page as it scrolls.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's title. It wraps, balanced across its lines, and is never cut short.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The title's heading level: 1 for the page's own heading, a lower level for a header inside a pane or a section that sits under another heading. It looks the same at every level.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title, in the smaller muted text, such as what the page is for.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: The trail to the page, usually Breadcrumbs with wrap={false}, above the title.

props.name: start
props.description: Before the title: an Avatar, an icon or a back IconButton.

props.name: meta
props.description: Beside the title, wrapping with it: Badges, such as a status, or a count.

props.name: actions
props.description: The page's actions, at the end of the title row: its primary action last. Below 32 rem of the header's own width they move under the title and wrap.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: A second row under the title: search, filters and view switches, laid out with `<Stack direction="row" wrap justify="between">`; see Toolbar's layouts.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Keeps the header in view at the top of the page as it scrolls, at `--env-frame-sticky-top`, under the app frame's header. Its height is published on its Page as `--env-page-header-block-size`, so content can stick below both.

props.name: controlSize
props.description: The size of the buttons and icon buttons in `actions` and `toolbar` that set none: sm for a dense page, such as one in a small window, or md. Give fields in the toolbar the same `size`.

Pager.Next.description: The destination after this one: a native link with rel="next", its title under the label Up next (EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.next), and an optional icon after them. It also stands alone, outside Pager.Root.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination; the link renders through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: children
props.description: The destination's title, such as the name of the next page. It shows below the direction label, wraps between words, and names the link after the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon, such as ArrowBack, before the previous destination's text, or such as ArrowForward, after the next one's; none by default.

props.name: rel
props.description: The link's relation to this page.

Pager.Previous.description: The destination before this one: a native link with rel="prev", its title under the label Previous (EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.previous), and an optional icon before them. It also stands alone, outside Pager.Root.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination; the link renders through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: children
props.description: The destination's title, such as the name of the next page. It shows below the direction label, wraps between words, and names the link after the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon, such as ArrowBack, before the previous destination's text, or such as ArrowForward, after the next one's; none by default.

props.name: rel
props.description: The link's relation to this page.

Pager.Root.description: A centered pair of previous and next destinations in a navigation landmark, from the previous and next props or from Pager.Previous and Pager.Next children; either one can be left out, and without any it renders nothing.

props.name: previous
props.description: The destination before this page, as the props of Pager.Previous; leave it out, or pass null, on the first page of a sequence.

props.name: next
props.description: The destination after this page, as the props of Pager.Next; leave it out, or pass null, on the last page of a sequence.

props.name: children
props.description: Pager.Previous and Pager.Next, instead of the previous and next props or beside one of them: they render between the previous prop's link and the next prop's, so the links keep their order.

props.name: aria-label
props.default: 'Previous and next content', or EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.label
props.description: The navigation landmark's name; give each pager its own where a page has several.

Pagination.description: A compact pager for toolbars: the range of items shown, such as 1–60 of 245, and icon buttons for the previous and next pages, in a navigation landmark. The application loads the pages; the range is announced as it changes, and focus stays on the button pressed.

props.name: page
props.description: The page shown, counted from 1. It is kept within the pages that exist, so a page beyond the end shows the last one.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: The most items a page shows, such as 60; at least 1.

props.name: total
props.description: All items, when known; the range then ends with it, as in 1–60 of 245, and the last page ends the list. Leave it out for a list read in batches, where hasNextPage says when it ends.

props.name: hasNextPage
props.description: Whether a later page exists, for a list without total, such as from a cursor's has more.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Receives the page before or after the current one when its button is pressed. The application loads that page and passes it back as page.

props.name: pending
props.description: A page is loading: the button pressed shows a spinner, also when the load starts in an effect after the page changes, and both buttons ignore presses while staying focusable. A load for another reason, such as a refresh, makes both wait without a spinner.

props.name: hideWhenSinglePage
props.description: Render nothing while every item fits on one page, so neither button has anywhere to go.

props.name: formatRange
props.default: 1–60 of 245, or 61–120 without total, with numbers in the locale
props.description: Writes the range from the first and last item shown, the total, the page and the page count, for one pager; EnvUIProvider's messages.pagination.range writes it for every pager.

props.name: previousLabel
props.description: The previous button's accessible name and tooltip.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: The next button's accessible name and tooltip.

props.name: variant
props.description: The buttons' variant, as on IconButton, such as text for a quiet toolbar.

props.name: size
props.description: The buttons' height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, they take the control height of the container, md unless the container sets another.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The navigation landmark's name, such as Report pages, where a page has more than one.

PanelDock.description: Panels docked to the bottom inline-end edge of a region, beside the page, for items people work on alongside it, such as drafts and conversations: open panels side by side, one maximized panel filling the region, and minimized panels as chips. A panel's content stays mounted through every change of mode and order.

props.name: panels
props.description: The panels in order, each a PanelDockPanel: open panels sit side by side, the newest at the end, and chips follow in the same order. The application owns them.

props.name: children
props.description: Renders a panel's content from its panel, such as a PanelDockHeader above the panel's body. The content mounts once and stays mounted until the panel closes.

props.name: onModeChange
props.description: Called with the mode a panel asks for, from its window controls and its chip, and from the dock itself with overflow="minimize".

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called from a panel's close control and its chip's close button.

props.name: onActivate
props.description: Called when people press or focus inside a panel that is not active, and when its chip brings it back.

props.name: onHeightChange
props.description: Called with a panel's new height in pixels when a drag on its top edge ends, and on each key press there.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: A width, 40rem by default, or a number of pixels, such as 600 or "600": while the dock itself is narrower, one panel at a time fills it and the others wait as chips. The dock then has data-stacked.

props.name: onStackedChange
props.description: Called with true when the dock stacks and with false when its panels sit side by side.

props.name: overflow
props.description: What the dock does when its open panels cannot all sit side by side at their minimum widths: scroll (default) scrolls the row sideways; minimize asks onModeChange to minimize the least recently active open panel, one at a time, until the rest fit, and to open it again once the region widens and it fits. It never asks for the active panel, the newest one or the one that holds focus, so never for a panel alone in the row, and where those cannot fit by themselves the row scrolls instead.

props.name: minimizedLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the list of chips, which holds minimized panels and the panels a stacked dock leaves out.

props.name: showLabel
props.default: Show and the text, such as Show Budget
props.description: Accessible name of a chip's button that shows its panel, from the chip's text. A function, as each chip names its own panel; PanelDockControls takes plain strings.

props.name: closeLabel
props.default: Close and the text, such as Close Budget
props.description: Accessible name of a chip's close button, from the chip's text.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.default: Resize and the title, such as Resize Quarterly report
props.description: Accessible name of a panel's resize handle, from its title.

PanelDockControls.description: Minimize, Maximize or Restore, and Close for the panel around it, as small icon buttons with tooltips. A stacked dock already fills the region, so its panels leave out Maximize.

props.name: minimizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the control that minimizes the panel to a chip.

props.name: maximizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the control that maximizes the panel to fill the region.

props.name: restoreLabel
props.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the same control on a maximized panel, which returns it.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the control that closes the panel.

PanelDockHeader.description: The header of a docked panel. It sticks to the top of the panel while its content scrolls: the title and its metadata at the start, the application's actions and the window controls at the end, small like a title bar's.

props.name: title
props.description: The panel's title, as a heading in 1.125 rem medium-weight text; it wraps between words rather than truncating.

props.name: meta
props.description: Supporting text below the title, in 0.875 rem muted text, such as who changed it last.

props.name: actions
props.description: The application's own actions, before the window controls, such as an Edit IconButton and a Menu of more; icon-only text buttons take the window controls' quiet icon color.

props.name: controls
props.description: The window controls: PanelDockControls inside a PanelDock by default. null leaves them out, and an element replaces them, such as PanelDockControls with translated labels.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The title's heading level in the page outline; the look stays the same.

props.name: children
props.description: Content below the title row that stays with the sticky header, such as Tabs.

Popover.description: A floating panel beside its trigger, for details or a small form: it opens on press, moves focus into itself, and closes with Esc, a press outside or when focus leaves it. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the popover's surface.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The control that opens and closes the popover, such as a Button or an IconButton. It must take a ref and props: it receives the press handler, aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.

props.name: title
props.description: A heading at the top, such as the name of what the popover describes; it names the popover.

props.name: children
props.description: The popover's content, or a function that receives close, for an action inside it that should close the popover once it is done, such as a form's submit.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The popover's accessible name when it has no title, such as Rename document.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of the trigger the popover opens on: top, bottom, left, right, or inline-start and inline-end, which follow the text direction. It flips to the other side without room.

props.name: align
props.description: How the popover lines up with the trigger along that side: its start, center or end.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether a controlled popover is open; update it from onOpenChange.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled popover starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Receives the requested state, and why, each time the popover asks to open or close: from the trigger, Esc, a press outside, focus leaving it or close (`close-press`).

props.name: width
props.description: The popover's width: md, 20 rem, for details and a field or two; lg, 28 rem, for a longer form. Both narrow to fit the window.

Progress.description: How much of a task is done, such as an upload or an import: a label, an optional value and a bar, exposed as a progress bar. Pass value null while the amount of work is unknown, and the bar sweeps instead.

props.name: value
props.description: How much of the task is done, between min and max, such as 40 of 100; null while the amount of work is unknown, which shows an indeterminate bar announced as Loading.

props.name: segments
props.description: Splits the track into this many equal steps, such as 4 for a task of four stages, each filling in turn. Without it, the track is one bar.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar shows, such as Seats assigned; it is visible above the bar and names it.

props.name: min
props.description: The low end of the range.

props.name: max
props.description: The high end of the range.

props.name: valueText
props.description: The value as text at the end of the label's row, formatted by the application, such as 2 of 5 or 40%. Without it, no value shows.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: The value as assistive technology reads it, with its unit in words, such as 2 of 5 seats. Without it, a screen reader reads the value as a percentage of the range, in the locale of the nearest EnvUIProvider.

Radio.description: One option of a RadioGroup: a native radio input with its label, and an optional description.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native radio input, so that a form library can register it and focus it; the other native props reach it too.

props.name: className
props.description: The option's class, on its root element, the label around the radio and the text.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the root element.

props.name: value
props.description: The value the group reports and a form submits when this option is chosen.

props.name: label
props.description: The option's visible name, such as Private; pressing it chooses the option.

props.name: description
props.description: A short, muted line under the label that helps people choose, such as Only the people you invite. It is part of the option's label, so it is read with its name.

RadioGroup.description: A set of options to choose exactly one from: a native fieldset whose legend names the group, with Radio options inline or as selectable rows.

props.name: ref
props.description: The group's fieldset.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's visible name, such as Visibility, as the fieldset's legend above the options. It names the group for assistive technology; without it, use aria-label or aria-labelledby.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of the chosen option in a controlled group; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value of the option an uncontrolled group starts with; a native form reset returns to it. Without value or defaultValue, no option is chosen until people choose one.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the option people choose.

props.name: name
props.description: The name every radio of the group submits its value under. Set it in a form; without it the group takes a unique generated name, so its radios still work as one group.

props.name: required
props.description: Require a choice before the form submits, through native constraint validation.

props.name: orientation
props.description: How the options are laid out: horizontal, radios before their labels side by side that wrap onto more lines; or vertical, connected selectable rows that fill the width, with the label and description at the start and the radio at the end, for options that need explaining.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every option of the group; a disabled group can't be focused or changed.

Rating.description: A read-only rating, such as a review score: stars filled to the value in half steps in the warning tone, with an optional number before them, named once for assistive technology as an image, such as "4.5 out of 5 stars". It shows a rating; it does not ask for one.

props.name: value
props.description: The rating, from 0 to max, such as 4.5. It shows rounded to the nearest half star, kept within 0 and max; a value that is not a number, such as NaN, shows no stars filled.

props.name: max
props.description: How many stars the scale has, as a whole number, such as 10. A fraction rounds to the nearest whole star; a value below 1 or not a number shows 5 stars.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the rating as a number before the stars, such as 4.5, in tabular digits and the locale's number format, such as 4,5 in German. The number is the rounded value the stars show, and it is hidden from assistive technology, since the stars' name already says it.

props.name: formatLabel
props.description: Writes the accessible name of the stars from the shown value, rounded to a half star, and the number of stars. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.rating.label`, which receives both as text in the locale's number format.

RelativeTime.description: A moment in a time element as text relative to now, such as "3 hours ago", with the date and time in a tooltip. One shared clock keeps every RelativeTime on the page current.

props.name: value
props.description: The moment to describe: a Date, milliseconds since 1970 or a date string such as an ISO 8601 timestamp. An invalid moment renders nothing.

props.name: now
props.description: A fixed moment to compare with, for tests and server rendering; the text then stays as it is. Without it, or with an invalid one, the text follows the current time.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Show the date and time in a tooltip on hover, such as "Oct 14, 2026, 9:41 AM", in the reader's time zone and the locale. Turn it off where the exact moment shows nearby. Inside an application's own Tooltip, that one describes the time instead.

props.name: locale
props.default: EnvUIProvider's locale for RelativeTime, else the runtime's language: the browser's, or the server's while rendering there
props.description: The language of the text, and of the date and time in RelativeTime's tooltip, as a BCP 47 tag such as "en-GB" or "de", or a list of them in order of preference.

props.name: format
props.description: How long the words are, from Intl.RelativeTimeFormat: long "3 hours ago", short "3 hr. ago" or narrow "3h ago", in the locale's own wording.

props.name: nowLabel
props.default: 'just now' or 'now' in English, the locale's word for now elsewhere
props.description: Text for a moment less than 45 seconds away, past or coming, such as "moments ago". English says "just now" of a past moment and "now" of a coming one; other languages the locale's word. RelativeTime takes EnvUIProvider's `messages.relativeTime.now` without it.

RichText.description: Saved rich text, read-only: Markdown rendered with the editor's own schema and parser, so it shows what RichTextEditor wrote, references included, with envUI's links, code and checkboxes. It renders on the server too.

props.name: children
props.description: The Markdown to show, such as what RichTextEditor saved.

props.name: extensions
props.description: Tiptap extensions added to the shared schema, such as a custom mark. They must parse and write Markdown, and the array must stay the same between renders, such as at module scope; a new array starts a new editing session. Pass the same extensions to RichText.

props.name: renderReference
props.type: (reference: RichTextReference, context: { readOnly: boolean; selected: boolean }) => ReactNode
props.default: the trigger and the label, such as #Launch
props.description: Renders a reference's content, such as an avatar beside the name; it receives whether the document is read-only and whether the reference is selected.

props.name: onReferenceClick
props.description: Called when people activate a reference, with the reference and the event, such as to open the record. A reference with an href is a link, which the editor never follows while it is editable; without an href, this makes the reference a button.

props.name: onLinkClick
props.description: Called when people activate a link in the document, with its href and the event: a native MouseEvent in the editor, a React mouse event in RichText. The editor never follows links while editable; call preventDefault to keep RichText or a read-only editor from following it.

RichTextEditor.description: A labelled editor for formatted text that people edit as it looks, built on Tiptap, with a formatting toolbar, references typed with a trigger such as

props.name: hint
props.description: Lasting guidance under the editor, such as a format or a limit, linked to it as its description.

props.name: value
props.description: The Markdown of a controlled editor; update it from onValueChange. A new value from outside, such as another draft, replaces the document and keeps the caret where it can.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The Markdown an uncontrolled editor starts with, and returns to when its form resets.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the document as Markdown after every edit, normalized by the editor's schema, so it can differ from the Markdown it was given, such as * for _ around italics.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the Markdown with a native form under this name, through a hidden input.

props.name: form
props.description: The ID of the form the hidden input belongs to, where the editor sits outside it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown in an empty document, such as what to write.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Makes the editor unavailable: it cannot be edited or focused, the toolbar is disabled, its value is left out of form submission and it takes the shared disabled opacity.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Shows the document without editing it: the toolbar is disabled and the document cannot be focused, but its links and references can, and the form still submits its value.

props.name: toolbar
props.default: every command, from heading to table
props.description: The toolbar's commands, in order, or false for no toolbar; Undo and Redo, and Attach files with onUpload, follow them.

props.name: references
props.description: Kinds of references people insert by typing a trigger, such as @ for people and # for topics, each with its own lookup. Triggers must be unique, and the array must stay the same between renders, such as at module scope.

props.name: slashCommands
props.description: Typing / opens a menu of block commands: true offers heading, the lists, quote, code block and table; an array adds the application's commands after them. A / reference source can't be used beside it.

props.name: onRequestLink
props.description: Opens the application's own link picker for Insert link, with the selected text, instead of the built-in dialog. Return the link, null to cancel, or a promise of either. A selection becomes a link to its href; at the caret, the label is inserted as the link's text.

props.name: onUpload
props.type: (file: File, request: { signal: AbortSignal }) => RichTextAttachment | null | Promise<RichTextAttachment | null>
props.description: Uploads a file people chose with Attach files, which shows in the toolbar only with this. Return where it lives as an attachment, null to skip it, or a promise of either; the signal aborts when the editor becomes read-only or disabled, or when a controlled value changes.

props.name: accept
props.description: The file types Attach files offers, as in a file input's accept, such as "image/*,.pdf".

props.name: multiple
props.description: Lets people choose several files at once with Attach files.

props.name: variant
props.description: The editor's look: outlined, the document in a bordered well on the field background, or plain, without a border or fill. quiet is accepted for the shared field type, but draws as outlined.

props.name: extensions
props.description: Tiptap extensions added to the shared schema, such as a custom mark. They must parse and write Markdown, and the array must stay the same between renders, such as at module scope; a new array starts a new editing session. Pass the same extensions to RichText.

props.name: renderReference
