props.type: (reference: RichTextReference, context: { readOnly: boolean; selected: boolean }) => ReactNode
props.default: the trigger and the label, such as #Launch
props.description: Renders a reference's content, such as an avatar beside the name; it receives whether the document is read-only and whether the reference is selected.

props.name: onReferenceClick
props.description: Called when people activate a reference, with the reference and the event, such as to open the record. A reference with an href is a link, which the editor never follows while it is editable; without an href, this makes the reference a button.

props.name: onLinkClick
props.description: Called when people activate a link in the document, with its href and the event: a native MouseEvent in the editor, a React mouse event in RichText. The editor never follows links while editable; call preventDefault to keep RichText or a read-only editor from following it.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

SearchField.description: A search input with a search icon and, while it has a query, a clear button; Esc also clears. Its label is hidden by default, so it sits beside buttons with a placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's accessible name, such as Search members. It shows as a floating label only with showLabel; otherwise a placeholder gives the visible guidance.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label in the field, as TextField does. A search field leaves it out, so that it sits in a toolbar with a placeholder such as Search.

props.name: value
props.description: The query of a controlled field; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The query an uncontrolled field starts with, and that a form reset restores.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the next query as people type, and an empty string when the clear button or Esc clears it.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The accessible name and tooltip of the clear button.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native input, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-text-field.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text before the value, such as the start of an address. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the field takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another, as a table cell does. A button beside a field takes the field's size. Floating and underline fields have their own height.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look: outline, with a thin border, at the control height; floating, an outlined field 3.5 rem tall whose label rests inside and floats into the outline, for long forms on a page; underline, as tall, with no border or fill and an underline on hover and focus; or ghost, only its text and start icon at rest, with a soft fill under the pointer and while focused and a placeholder that clears on focus, for a search at the top of a sidebar or a list.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text after the value, such as a unit. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

SearchTrigger.description: The button that opens search or a command palette: a field-like button with its label and the shortcut's keys, or a search icon alone. It presses itself when the shortcut is pressed, and the application opens the search from onClick.

props.name: label
props.description: The label, and the name of the icon-only trigger.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: The keyboard shortcut, shown as keys at the end and announced as aria-keyshortcuts: `mod+k` is ⌘K on Apple platforms and Ctrl+K elsewhere. false shows and handles none.

props.name: listen
props.description: Press the trigger when the shortcut is pressed anywhere in the window, text fields included. With several triggers listening for one shortcut, the most recently mounted one that is visible and not behind a modal dialog takes it. A disabled trigger, or a key press that something else already handled, such as an editor's own shortcut, leaves the key alone.

props.name: iconOnly
props.default: true inside a sidebar showing icons only, else false
props.description: Show only the search icon, in a ghost IconButton with the label and shortcut in a tooltip.

props.name: tooltipSide
props.default: 'inline-end' inside a sidebar showing icons only, else 'bottom'
props.description: The side of the trigger the icon-only tooltip opens on.

props.name: size
props.default: the container's control height, md unless the container sets another
props.description: The height, as on every control.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the width of the container, such as at the top of a sidebar.

SegmentedControl.description: One choice among a few items on a pill rail, such as views or filters of the same content; the chosen item takes the primary colors. A radio group, with one tab stop and arrow keys.

props.name: items
props.description: The items, two to five, in the order they show.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen item's value. The control is always controlled: update it from onValueChange.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the item people choose, by pressing it or with the arrow keys.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The group's accessible name, such as Work items; the control has no visible label.

props.name: size
props.description: The rail's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale, so it lines up with buttons and fields of the same size. Without it, the rail takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the available width, split evenly between the items; a label too long for its share is cut short with an ellipsis and shows whole in a tooltip. Without it the control is as wide as its items, and scrolls in a container too narrow for them.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every item; the control can't be focused or changed.

Select.description: One choice from a list that stays collapsed until opened: a Button trigger that shows the chosen option and opens a popup list, where a check mark shows the chosen option, with a label above it, a description, an error and native form participation.

props.name: ref
props.description: The trigger, the button that shows the chosen option and opens the list.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-select.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element.

props.name: items
props.description: The options of the list, in order, each with a value, a label and whether it is disabled.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen option's value in a controlled select, or null for none, which shows the placeholder; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The chosen option's value an uncontrolled select starts with; a native form reset returns to it. Without it, nothing is chosen and the trigger shows the placeholder.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the option people choose.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the chosen option's value with a form under this name, through a hidden input.

props.name: required
props.description: Require a choice before the form submits: the browser refuses the form and moves focus to the trigger while nothing is chosen.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: What the trigger shows while nothing is chosen, such as Choose an owner.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: A hint for the browser's autofill, such as country, set on the hidden input.

props.name: variant
props.description: The trigger's Button variant, to suit its surroundings: secondary, a filled pill, for the page; or outline, a bordered pill, for panes, dialogs, rows and toolbars, where a fill would blend with the surface.

props.name: size
props.description: The trigger's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the trigger takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another. The popup's rows take the row height of the scale.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

Skeleton.description: A placeholder in the shape of content that is loading, such as a line of text or a row: a block with rounded corners on the neutral fill, which pulses unless people prefer reduced motion. It is hidden from assistive technology; put placeholders in a LoadingState, which names the region.

props.name: width
props.description: The placeholder's width, as a CSS length, such as 38% or 12rem, for the content it stands for. Without it, the placeholder fills the width of its container.

props.name: height
props.description: The placeholder's height, as a CSS length, such as 1.25rem for a heading or 3.5rem for a row.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: How strong the fill is: muted, the neutral fill, or default, one step stronger, for a placeholder that stands out among the others, such as a title.

Slider.description: A value in a range, chosen by dragging a thumb along a track, pressing the track or with the keyboard, with its label and current value above the track and an optional description below.

props.name: label
props.description: The value's name above the track, such as Opacity. It names the slider, and pressing it moves focus to the slider.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the track, such as what the value applies to, linked to the slider as its description.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of a controlled slider; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value an uncontrolled slider starts with; a native form reset returns to it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value while it changes, by dragging, pressing the track or with the keyboard, as often as the thumb moves.

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.description: Receives the value once a change is complete: when the thumb is released or the track pressed, and after each key. Use it for work that runs once per change, such as saving.

props.name: min
props.description: The lowest value, at the start of the track.

props.name: max
props.description: The highest value, at the end of the track.

props.name: step
props.description: The distance between the values the slider can take, counted from min; an arrow key moves by it.

props.name: largeStep
props.default: a tenth of the range in whole steps, at least one step
props.description: The change of Page Up, Page Down and an arrow key with Shift.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: The value as people read it above the track and assistive technology announces it, such as (value) => `${value}%`. Without it, the number shows in the locale.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the shown number: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dim the slider; it can't be focused or moved, and forms leave it out.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the value with a form under this name.

props.name: form
props.description: The id of a form the slider belongs to when it sits outside of it.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: The native range input, for example to focus it.

Spinner.description: Work of unknown length in a small area, such as a panel that is updating: an arc in the control blue that turns, and keeps turning slowly with a reduced-motion preference. With a label it is a progress bar named by it; without one it is hidden from assistive technology. The hook --env-spinner-color recolors it, such as to a button's label color.

props.name: label
props.description: The work it stands for, such as Refreshing members, which names the spinner as a progress bar for assistive technology. Leave it out where a busy control or region already says so; the spinner is then hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: size
props.description: sm, 1 rem, inside controls and beside a line of text; md, 1.5 rem, beside a heading or in a panel; or lg, 3 rem, in the middle of a region whose content is on its way.

SplitPane.Pane.description: One of the two panes. It scrolls on its own when the split pane has a size of its own.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the pane, which makes it a region landmark that people can jump to, such as Documents. Name the panes of a page's main layout; leave small panes unnamed.

SplitPane.ResizeHandle.description: The handle between the panes: a focusable separator that the pointer drags and the arrow keys move, which names the first pane in aria-controls. A double click returns it to the default size. A stacked split pane has none.

props.name: label
props.description: The handle's name, which says what it resizes, such as Resize document list.

SplitPane.Root.description: Two panes and a handle between them that resizes them, by pointer and keyboard (the APG window splitter). Below `stackBelow` of its own width the panes stack and the handle goes.

props.name: orientation
props.description: How the panes sit: horizontal, side by side with the first at the inline start, or vertical, one above the other. A vertical split pane needs a height of its own.

props.name: size
props.description: The first pane's size in `unit`, for a controlled split pane.

props.name: defaultSize
props.description: The first pane's size in `unit` until people choose one, or one is stored under `persist`.

props.name: onSizeChange
props.description: Receives each new size of the first pane, in `unit`: while dragging with committed false, and with committed true as a drag ends, a key moves the handle or a double click resets it.

props.name: minSize
props.description: The first pane's smallest size, in `unit`.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: The first pane's largest size, in `unit`.

props.name: unit
props.description: The unit of the sizes: %, a share of the split pane's width (height when vertical), or rem, a length that follows the reader's text size, such as a list that keeps its width as the window grows.

props.name: persist
props.description: Keeps the size people choose under this localStorage key, for an uncontrolled split pane; a double click on the handle forgets it. It is read after the first render, so server markup and hydration agree.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: A width, such as '44rem', or a number of pixels: while the split pane itself is narrower, its panes stack, the first above the second, the handle goes and the root has data-stacked. It follows the split pane's own width, not the window's, so a split pane in a narrow column stacks too. A container query stacks the server's markup before any script runs.

props.name: onStackedChange
props.description: Receives true when the panes stack and false when they sit side by side again.

props.name: children
props.description: The panes and the handle between them: Pane, ResizeHandle, Pane.

Stack.description: A layout of its direct children in a column, or a row, a step of the spacing scale apart, so the parent owns the space between them and the children need no margins.

props.name: direction
props.description: The direction the children run in: column, one under another, or row, side by side, such as a form's actions.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Let a row wrap onto more lines when its children don't fit, as a row of actions does.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space between the direct children, as a step of the spacing scale: 1 is 0.25 rem, 2 is 0.5 rem, 3 is 0.75 rem, 4 is 1 rem, 5 is 1.5 rem, 6 is 2 rem, 7 is 2.5 rem, 8 is 3 rem and 9 is 4 rem; 0 removes it.

props.name: align
props.description: How the children line up across the stack: stretch makes each as wide as a column (as tall as a row), except controls such as buttons, which keep their own size; start, center and end keep every child at its own size, at that side or in the middle.

props.name: justify
props.description: Where the children sit along the stack when there is room to spare: at the start, in the center, at the end, such as a form's actions at its end, or between, spread out with the first and last at the edges.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<section />} or render={<footer />}, or another component to lay out as the stack without a wrapper, such as a Surface or a Theme: the stack's class, gap and alignment merge into its props. It must forward native props and refs. A div by default.

Stat.Group.description: Stats on one surface, a pane's fill by default, in as many even columns as fit; they wrap as space runs out. Use the muted background for a group on a pane. A group named with aria-label or aria-labelledby is exposed as a group, so assistive technology announces the name.

props.name: background
props.description: The group's fill, as for Surface: default on the page, or muted for a group on a pane, so its stats stand apart; page or raised where those fit.

props.name: padding
props.default: 1.25 rem in narrow windows, growing to 1.5 rem from 50 rem wide
props.description: The inset on every side, as a step of the spacing scale, such as 4 for 1 rem; 0 removes it. Without it, the inset follows the window's width, as for Surface.

Stat.Root.description: A labelled key figure for a dashboard, such as Active projects 128, with an optional trend and description. It has no surface of its own; Stat.Group puts several on one, or a Card holds one.

props.name: label
props.description: What the figure measures, such as Active projects, in muted text above it.

props.name: value
props.description: The figure, formatted by the application with its unit, such as 1,284 or 2.5 days, or an AnimatedNumber that rolls to new values. It shows large, in tabular digits.

props.name: description
props.description: A muted note below the figure, after the trend, such as the period: Last 30 days.

props.name: trend
props.description: The change since an earlier period, such as up and +12% from last month, shown below the figure as a direction icon and text in its tone.

Surface.description: A container with a background, an inset and corners, but no layout of its own: spacing between its children, alignment and behaviour come from what it holds, such as a Stack. Card and other containers build on it.

props.name: background
props.description: The fill: default, the background of panes and side regions; muted, the background of rows; page, the page background; or raised, a block that stands out on a pane.

props.name: padding
props.default: 1.25 rem in narrow windows, growing to 1.5 rem from 50 rem wide
props.description: The inset on every side, as a step of the spacing scale, from 1 (0.25 rem) to 9 (4 rem), such as 5 for 1.5 rem; 0 removes it. Without it, the inset follows the window's width.

props.name: radius
props.description: The corner radius: xl, the large 1.75 rem corners of panes; sm, 0.5 rem for small blocks; full, fully rounded ends for a toolbar or a bar of filters; or none, square, for a region that meets the edges of its container.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render the surface as, for its meaning, such as render={<section />}, or another component to render it onto without a wrapper, such as a Stack that lays out its content: the surface's class, style and attributes merge into its props. It must forward native props and refs. A div by default.

Switch.description: An on/off setting that takes effect at once: a native checkbox with the switch role, drawn as a track and a thumb, with its label beside it.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native checkbox with the switch role, so that a form library can register it and focus it; the other native props, such as name, reach it too.

props.name: className
props.description: The switch's class, on its root element, the label around the track and the text.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the root element.

props.name: label
props.description: The setting the switch turns on or off, such as Show completed tasks, beside the track. It names the switch, stays the same in both states, and pressing it toggles the switch too. Without it, name the switch with aria-label or aria-labelledby.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether a controlled switch is on; update it from onCheckedChange.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled switch starts on; a native form reset returns it to this state.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Receives the new state each time people turn the switch on or off.

Table.Body.description: The data rows of a table, a native tbody, separated by hairlines.

Table.Cell.description: A data cell, a native td, with a label that names its value while rows stack.

props.name: label
props.description: The column's name, shown before the value while a table with narrowLayout="stack" stacks its rows. Assistive technology reads the column header instead.

props.name: align
props.description: Aligns the content with the start or the end of the cell.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures aligned to the end, for numbers that compare down a column. In a sortable header the arrow comes before the label, so the label lines up with the numbers.

props.name: nowrap
props.description: Keeps the content on one line. In a table with set column widths, content that doesn't fit ends with an ellipsis.

Table.Head.description: The header rows of a table, a native thead, which hold the column headers.

Table.HeaderCell.description: A header cell, a native th that heads its column, or its row with scope="row". With onSortChange it sorts its column; in a table with resizable columns it holds the column's resize handle.

props.name: sortDirection
props.description: The column's sort order: aria-sort on the header and the arrow in its sort button. Use it with onSortChange; without it only sets aria-sort.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: The header becomes a button across the cell that asks the application to sort the rows by this column, with the order pressing it asks for: descending while the column is sorted ascending, ascending otherwise. The application sorts the rows and sets sortDirection.

props.name: sortLabel
props.default: '{header} sort {next order}', from EnvUIProvider's messages.table.sortAscending and sortDescending
props.description: Accessible name of the sort button, which says what pressing it does: the header's name followed by "sort ascending", or by "sort descending" while the column is sorted ascending.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the column's resize handle, "Resize" followed by the header's name.

props.name: align
props.description: Aligns the content with the start or the end of the cell.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures aligned to the end, for numbers that compare down a column. In a sortable header the arrow comes before the label, so the label lines up with the numbers.

props.name: nowrap
props.description: Keeps the content on one line. In a table with set column widths, content that doesn't fit ends with an ellipsis.

Table.Root.description: A semantic data table on a rounded surface, in a focusable region that scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the table and its scroll region when there is no caption. A table needs a caption, an aria-label or an aria-labelledby, which names its region too.

props.name: caption
props.description: A visible caption above the rows that names the table and its scroll region, in place of aria-label or aria-labelledby. Under a sticky header it scrolls away with the rows.

props.name: density
props.description: How tightly the rows pack: xs, sm, md or lg changes only the cells' block padding, never the text. Buttons, icon buttons and fields in the cells take the small control height in every density, unless they set a size.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: The header row stays at the top of the region while the rows scroll beneath it. The region then scrolls vertically too, so give it a height through regionClassName or the surrounding layout.

props.name: regionClassName
props.description: Class of the scroll region around the table, for example to limit its height.

props.name: narrowLayout
props.description: What the table does when its region is narrower than stackBelow: scroll keeps the columns and scrolls sideways; stack shows each body row as a block that starts with its first cell, followed by the other cells with their labels. The header row is then visually hidden.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: The region width below which a table with narrowLayout="stack" stacks its rows: a CSS length such as 60rem or 480px, or a number of pixels, such as 600 or "600". Wide tables, such as seven sortable columns, need more.

props.name: onStackedChange
props.description: Called with true when the rows stack and with false when the columns return, from the same measurement as stackBelow, for example to show another sort control while the header row is hidden; a table that leaves while its rows stack reports false. The region has data-stacked while the rows stack.

props.name: columnWidths
props.description: Column widths in percent of the table width, in column order and adding up to 100, for widths the application controls with onColumnWidthsChange. Set widths fix the columns: long words wrap and nowrap cells end with an ellipsis.

props.name: defaultColumnWidths
props.description: Starting column widths, in percent, when the table owns them; other defaults start them over. Double-clicking a resize handle restores them, or else the widths a controlled table started with.

props.name: onColumnWidthsChange
props.description: Called with every column's width when people resize a column.

props.name: minColumnWidths
props.description: Smallest width of each column in percent, in column order, or one value for every column.

props.name: resizableColumns
props.description: People can resize the columns with a handle at the end of each header cell but the last, which moves the boundary to the next column and keeps the table's width. Needs columnWidths or defaultColumnWidths.

Table.Row.description: A row of a table, a native tr, which can highlight on hover or be selected.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The row highlights on hover and while focus is inside it, for rows that open something through a link or button in a cell. It adds no behavior of its own.

props.name: selected
props.description: The row is selected: it reports aria-selected and takes the selection colors, with a bar at its start. Pass false to the other rows of a table whose rows can be selected; unset, a row reports no selection state.

Tabs.description: Switches between panels of related content in one place: a rail of the buttons you supply, each a tab linked to its panel, with selection from the keyboard and panels that fade as they change. The selected tab keeps its button's own look; the others are quiet on the rail.

props.name: items
props.description: The tabs in order, each with its value, button and panel content.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The tab list's accessible name, such as Project views.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected tab's value, for controlled tabs; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The tab that uncontrolled tabs start on.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the tab people select, by pressing it or from the keyboard.

props.name: activation
props.description: automatic selects a tab as the arrow keys move focus to it; manual only moves focus, and Enter or Space selects, for panels that take a moment to show.

props.name: orientation
props.description: horizontal puts the tabs in a row, moved through with the left and right arrow keys; vertical in a column, with the up and down arrow keys. The panels stay below the list either way.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description: Keep the panels of unselected tabs mounted and hidden, so their state, such as a draft or a scroll position, survives switching; otherwise a panel unmounts once it has faded out.

props.name: renderList
props.description: Places the tab list in a layout of your own, such as beside a heading: it receives the list and returns what to render in its place, with the list in it once. The panels stay below.

props.name: listClassName
props.description: A class for the tab list, the rail that holds the tabs.

props.name: panelClassName
props.description: A class for every panel.

props.name: fill
props.description: The selected panel takes the height left below the list, for content that fills a region, such as a canvas; give the tabs a height, for example as a flex child.

props.name: size
props.description: The rail's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. The tabs inside are a little shorter. lg gives tabs as tall as md buttons; sm suits a toolbar or a bar, beside a SegmentedControl or buttons of size sm.

Text.description: Semantic native text with typography and color from the shared token scale.

props.name: variant
props.description: The text style: display for a page's introduction, body for running text, headline for a page's heading, title for a section's, body-sm for supporting text and caption for the smallest notes. body-sm and caption are muted unless emphasis says otherwise.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: How strong the text is: default, the text color; muted, for supporting text; subtle, the weakest, for text that should recede, such as a hint beside a value.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<h2 />} for a heading or render={<span />} inside a line; a p by default. The text's class and attributes merge into its props.

TextField.description: A labelled single-line text input: a native input with a floating label, a description and an error, at the control height in an outline or ghost look, or taller as the floating and underline variants, with an optional start icon, end action, prefix and suffix.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native input, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-text-field.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value as people type, after the native onChange.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look: outline, with a thin border, at the control height; floating, an outlined field 3.5 rem tall whose label rests inside and floats into the outline, for long forms on a page; underline, as tall, with no border or fill and an underline on hover and focus; or ghost, only its text and start icon at rest, with a soft fill under the pointer and while focused and a placeholder that clears on focus, for a search at the top of a sidebar or a list.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: A decorative icon at the start of the field, such as Search or Mail.

props.name: endAction
props.description: A control at the end of the field, such as an IconButton that reveals or copies the value; name it with aria-label. A button that sets no variant takes ghost here.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label in the field, where it rests while the field is empty and floats into the outline while the field has focus or a value. Set false for a field whose purpose is clear without it, such as a search in a toolbar: the label still names the field for assistive technology, and a placeholder gives the visible guidance.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the field takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another, as a table cell does. A button beside a field takes the field's size. Floating and underline fields have their own height.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text before the value, such as the start of an address. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text after the value, such as a unit. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

Textarea.description: A labelled text area for text over several lines: a native textarea in the text field's frame, at a fixed height that scrolls and resizes from its bottom edge, or growing with its content.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native text area, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-text-field.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look, as TextField's: outline, underline or ghost. A text area is always tall, with its label resting at the top, so it has no floating variant.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the text as people type, after the native onChange.

props.name: sizing
props.description: How the height follows the text: fixed keeps its height, scrolls and resizes from the bottom edge, by dragging it or with the arrow keys; content grows and shrinks with the text.

props.name: rows
props.description: The lines the field shows: with fixed sizing, its height in rows, at least 7.5 rem; with content sizing, the lines it starts at and shrinks back to, also under 7.5 rem. Without rows, both start at 7.5 rem.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

Theme.description: An explicit, scoped theme: a color scheme, a contrast and a scale, which nested Themes and envUI's popups keep. Theme preference and persistence belong to the app.

props.name: theme
props.description: The color scheme.

props.name: contrast
props.description: `high` for the high-contrast colors; `standard` keeps the standard ones even while the system asks for more contrast; `system` follows `prefers-contrast: more`. Defaults to the contrast of the enclosing Theme, and to `system` outside any. It wins over a `data-env-contrast` attribute passed to the Theme; left out, such an attribute of `high` or `standard` sets the contrast, for the boundary, its nested Themes and its popups alike.

props.name: scale
props.description: The app scale of everything inside: comfortable, or compact for a desktop productivity app. Use one scale per app or window, and another only on a Theme around a whole region, such as a docked inspector. Defaults to the scale of the enclosing Theme, and to comfortable outside any. It wins over a `data-env-scale` attribute passed to the Theme.

ThemePreferenceProvider.description: Owns the theme preference: persistence, the system theme and document-root theming.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: localStorage key; match the bootstrap script's. Defaults to "env-theme".

props.name: defaultPreference
props.description: Used when nothing is stored. Defaults to "system".

props.name: applyToDocument
props.description: Theme the document root as well as this subtree (default). Root theming covers the page background, native controls, portals rendered by other libraries and the content of every theme-color meta tag, which takes the canvas color. One provider per document applies to it: pass false to any other, nested in it or beside it. In development, envUI reports two providers that both apply.

props.name: contrast
props.description: Contrast of the Theme boundary around the children, and of the document root with applyToDocument: high, standard, or system to follow `prefers-contrast: more`, as on Theme. Defaults to the contrast of an enclosing Theme; outside any, a provider applying to the document gives its boundary a contrast the page set on the root, and otherwise system. With system, the provider removes from the root only a contrast that envUI wrote and the page left unchanged: a provider, this one or one before it, or the bootstrap script. Pass a contrast that is fixed for the application to createThemeBootstrapScript too, so the root has it before the first paint.

props.name: scale
props.description: The app scale, comfortable or compact for a desktop productivity app, as on Theme: of the Theme boundary around the children, and, marked as envUI's own, of the document root with applyToDocument. Without it, the boundary takes the scale of an enclosing Theme; outside any, a provider applying to the document gives its boundary a scale the page set on the root, so the application, the page and its portals share it, and otherwise comfortable. The root keeps a scale the page set but drops one that envUI wrote and the page left unchanged. Pass the same scale to createThemeBootstrapScript so the root has it before the first paint.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the Theme boundary around the children.

ThemeRadioGroup.description: The theme choice for a Menu: System, Light and Dark as radio items. Inside a ThemePreferenceProvider it shows and stores the provider's preference; value and onValueChange connect it to a theme the application stores itself.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen preference: system, light or dark.

props.name: onValueChange
props.default: the nearest ThemePreferenceProvider's setPreference, which stores the choice
props.description: Called with the preference chosen, for an application that stores the theme itself.

props.name: label
props.description: A small heading above the choices, which names the group. Leave it out inside a submenu, which its row already names.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of a heading elsewhere in the menu that names the group, in place of label.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Close the menu after a choice. Off by default, so people see the theme change with the menu still open.

ThemeToggle.description: Switches between the light and dark themes and stores the choice.

props.name: size
props.description: As Button's: the height, and the width, of the square button.

props.name: variant
props.description: The emphasis, as Button's. Without it, the button takes the variant its container gives, such as ghost in a toolbar, and else secondary.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning, as Button's: accent on a primary button only, and danger on a primary, outline, ghost or text one. A secondary button is always neutral.

props.name: pending
props.description: As Button's: a spinner replaces the icon while the work runs.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The button's name; without it, Switch to dark theme or Switch to light theme, or EnvUIProvider's messages.themeToggle.

TitleBar.description: A window title bar without the application shell, for a start page or a simple window of an installed web app or desktop shell that draws its own title bar. It looks like AppShell's title bar: empty space drags the window, it leaves room for the window controls the system draws, and controls inside are small. It is a normal block; WindowFrame puts it above content that scrolls on its own.

props.name: start
props.description: Content at the inline start, such as the application mark and a Menubar.

props.name: children
props.description: Content centered in the bar, such as the document title.

props.name: end
props.description: Content at the inline end, such as actions; the window controls follow it.

Toast.Provider.description: Hosts the notifications that useToast shows: brief feedback at the edge of the window, announced and dismissed after a few seconds or by people. Put one near the root of the application; it renders a region for each placement in a portal, in the theme of the place it is rendered.

props.name: children
props.description: The application, or the part of it whose components call useToast.

props.name: defaultPlacement
props.description: Where notifications show unless show names a placement: bottom-end, stacking upward from the bottom corner at the end of the line, or top-center, stacking downward from the top.

props.name: visibleLimit
props.description: How many notifications each placement shows at once, a positive integer. The newest stay visible; older ones wait behind a count of hidden notifications and come back as newer ones close. Danger notifications always show, and take their places first.

Toolbar.Button.description: An icon-only button of a toolbar, named by its label, which a tooltip shows; disabled, it leaves the arrow keys' path.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon, such as FormatBold.

props.name: label
props.description: The action's name, such as Bold: assistive technology announces it, and the tooltip shows it on hover and focus.

props.name: pressed
props.description: For a button that turns something on and off, such as Bold: whether it is on. It is announced as pressed and drawn selected. Leave it out for a button that acts once, such as Undo.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: The keyboard shortcut that does the same, such as Ctrl+B, with keys joined by +: the tooltip shows it, and aria-keyshortcuts announces it, in ARIA's key names, such as Control+B. A sequence, such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+B, shows its keys without the attribute, as in Menu.

props.name: variant
props.description: As Button's; ghost by default, from the toolbar.

props.name: pending
props.description: As Button's: a spinner replaces the icon while the work runs.

Toolbar.Group.description: Controls of a toolbar that belong together, such as the text styles.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the group, such as Text style, where its controls belong together.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control in the group.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element to render the group as, such as a ButtonGroup.

Toolbar.Link.description: An icon-only link of a toolbar, named by its label, which a tooltip shows.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination, through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon, such as Help.

props.name: label
props.description: The destination's name, which assistive technology announces and the tooltip shows.

Toolbar.Root.description: A row, or a column, of controls for one subject, such as a text editor's formatting: one tab stop, with the arrow keys moving between its controls (the APG toolbar pattern). Buttons the application puts inside take the ghost variant unless they set another.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the toolbar for assistive technology, such as Formatting.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The direction the controls run in, and which arrow keys move between them.

props.name: size
props.description: The height of the buttons inside, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the control height of the container.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control inside.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: Whether the arrow keys move from the last control to the first and back.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element to render the toolbar as, such as a ButtonGroup that connects its buttons; the toolbar's class, attributes and keyboard handling merge into its props.

props.name: children
props.description: The controls: Toolbar.Button, Toolbar.Link, Toolbar.Group and Toolbar.Separator.

Toolbar.Separator.description: A line between groups of a toolbar's controls, across the toolbar's direction.

Tooltip.description: A short label beside a control, shown while the pointer rests on it or it has keyboard focus, such as an icon-only button's name or why a control is disabled. It closes on Esc and when the control is pressed. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the tooltip's popup.

props.name: content
props.description: What the tooltip shows: a short, supplementary text, such as an icon-only control's name or why a control is disabled. While it is open, a control with a name of its own is described by it (aria-describedby); never the only place essential information appears.

props.name: children
props.description: The one control it describes, such as an IconButton, which takes the trigger's props and ref. A disabled control is wrapped in an element that hovering opens the tooltip on. Around a button, link, tab or menu item, it is focusable and carries the control's name, role and state, reported disabled, so keyboard focus opens it too.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of the control it opens on: top, bottom, left, right, or inline-start and inline-end, which follow the text direction. Where the window has no room, it flips to the other side.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds the pointer rests on the control before the tooltip opens; keyboard focus opens it at once.

Tree.description: A virtualized tree of rows for large hierarchies such as file trees. The application passes the visible rows and owns expansion and selection; the tree owns focus, keyboard navigation and scrolling. It fills its parent's height, scrolls itself and renders only the rows in view.

props.name: items
props.description: The visible rows in order, flattened: an expanded row is followed by its visible descendants. The application owns expansion; collapsing a row removes its descendants from items.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The tree's accessible name, such as Files.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected row's id: it takes the navigation selection colors and scrolls into view when it changes. The application sets it, usually from onAction.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Called when people open a row: with preview true on a single click and Space, and false on a double click and Enter. Expandable rows call it too, and disabled rows don't.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Called with the row and its new state from a press on its chevron, the right arrow key on a collapsed row and the left arrow key on an expanded one, mirrored in right-to-left text. The application updates items.

props.name: contextMenu
props.description: Menu items for the row people right-click, or press Shift+F10 or the Menu key on, or for the tree's empty area when the item is null. Without it, the browser's own context menu stays.

props.name: contextMenuLabel
props.description: The context menu's accessible name.

props.name: density
props.description: How tightly the rows pack: xs, sm, md or lg changes only their block padding, never the text or the icons. In the comfortable scale sm rows are 1.75 rem tall and md rows 2.25 rem. Under a coarse pointer every row is at least 2.75 rem.

props.name: className
props.description: A class for the tree, the element that scrolls.

props.name: style
props.description: The tree's inline style, such as a height.

props.name: ref
props.description: The tree element, which scrolls and holds focus.

WindowFrame.description: A window without the application shell, such as a start page: it fills the window with the title bar on top and the content scrolling below it, so the window controls drawn over the title bar never cover a scrollbar. The keyboard scrolls the content as it would the document.

props.name: titleBar
props.description: The window's title bar at the top, typically a TitleBar.

props.name: children
props.description: The window's content, which scrolls below the title bar.

props.name: scrollRef
props.description: The element that scrolls the content, to read and restore scroll positions.

breakpointQuery.description: The media query for a viewport at least as wide as a breakpoint (`up`, the default), or narrower than it (`down`), so that `up` and `down` of one breakpoint never both match nor both miss: `breakpointQuery('md')` is `(width >= 48rem)`.

countDiffLines.description: How many lines a change adds and removes, as a DiffStat shows them.
countDiffLines.signature: (before: string, after: string, filename?: string): { additions: number; deletions: number; }

createRichTextExtensions.description: The Tiptap extensions RichTextEditor and RichText share: formatting, lists and task lists, tables, safe links and images, Markdown with raw HTML kept as text, a placeholder and references. options.extensions are added after them, for other Tiptap integrations that need the same schema.

createThemeBootstrapScript.description: Inline script for the document head. It themes the root element before the first paint, so a saved or system dark theme does not flash light while the application loads, and a high or standard contrast applies from the start.
createThemeBootstrapScript.signature: ({ storageKey, defaultPreference, contrast, scale, }?: ThemeBootstrapOptions): string

formatRelativeTime.description: A moment as text relative to another, by default the current time, such as "in 2 days", "3 hours ago" or "just now", through Intl.RelativeTimeFormat. An invalid moment gives an empty string; an invalid now is ignored, as by RelativeTime, for the current time.

useAppShell.description: Shell controls for content rendered inside AppShell.

useBreakpoint.description: Whether the viewport is at least as wide as a breakpoint: `useBreakpoint('md')` is true from 48 rem up. As useMediaQuery, it returns `defaultValue` on the server and while hydrating.

useContainerSize.description: The size of an element, kept up to date as it changes: its inline and block size in CSS pixels, along its writing mode, from a ResizeObserver. It is undefined on the server and until the element is measured, which happens before the browser paints it; an element that stops being rendered, such as one in a hidden tab panel, keeps its last size until it shows again. Pass a ref object, read once the element mounts, or the element itself, such as one kept in state by a callback ref. Prefer a container query (`@container`) where only styles change. const panel = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null); const size = useContainerSize(panel); const narrow = size !== undefined && size.inlineSize < 640;
useContainerSize.signature: <T extends Element>(target: RefObject<T | null> | T | null, options?: ContainerSizeOptions): ContainerSize | undefined

useLocale.description: The locale of the nearest EnvUIProvider, for formatting in step with envUI, or undefined where no provider sets one: the runtime's locale applies then.

useMediaQuery.description: Whether the viewport matches a media query, such as `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, kept up to date as it changes. It returns `defaultValue` on the server and while hydrating, then the browser's answer; a page rendered only in the browser gets the answer in its first render. Prefer CSS (`@media`, or `@container` for a component's own width) where the difference is only in styles.

useTheme.description: The theme of the nearest Theme, including across React portals: its color scheme, contrast and scale. A portal of the application's own takes it with `<Theme {...useTheme()}>`. A contrast of `system` leaves the choice to the stylesheet, which reads `prefers-contrast: more`.

useThemePreference.description: The theme preference from the nearest ThemePreferenceProvider.

useToast.description: Shows and dismisses notifications through the nearest Toast.Provider: show, dismiss and clear. Throws outside a provider.

tokens.usage: Use a token through its CSS custom property, such as var(--env-color-fg-muted), in CSS that styles the application. envUI components already use them; never restyle their classes.
